findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA for conflicts. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2

Order Form creates a different precedence regime from the MSA and says the Order Form prevails over every other document; the MSA does not define the Order Form as part of the Agreement, leaving its status and precedence uncertain. 01_msa.md sections 1.1 and 14.2; 05_order_form.md sections 2.1-2.2

Glossary says its definitions prevail over any other definition, but it is only Schedule 10 and is ranked below the MSA by the MSA/Order Form precedence provisions. 15_glossary.md section 1.2; 01_msa.md section 14.2; 05_order_form.md section 2.1
No clear hierarchy exists among Schedules of equal rank, yet many Schedules conflict with each other, leaving those conflicts unresolved. 05_order_form.md section 2.1(c); schedules generally
Agreement term conflicts: MSA initial term is 24 months, while Order Form initial term is 12 months from Service Commencement Date. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 1.2

SOW programme is 36 months, exceeding both the MSA 24-month initial term and the Order Form 12-month initial term without explaining survival or renewal dependency. 02_sow.md section 2.1; 01_msa.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 1.2

SOW programme commences on 1 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027 and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 02_sow.md section 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md section 7.3
Service commencement dates conflict: Order Form states 1 April 2027, while SOW programme commences 1 March 2027. 05_order_form.md section 1.3; 02_sow.md section 2.2
Convenience termination notice periods conflict: MSA requires 90 days, while SOW permits termination of the SOW on 30 days. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3

Renewal/non-renewal provisions conflict or overlap: MSA auto-renews unless terminated under clause 3.3 with 90 days' notice, while Order Form auto-renews unless 30 days' non-renewal notice is given. 01_msa.md sections 3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md sections 6.1-6.2
Monthly recurring charge conflicts: MSA says £12,400, SOW says £12,800, and Pricing Schedule says £13,100. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1; 10_pricing.md section 1.1

Annual Contract Value of £153,600 matches £12,800/month but conflicts with the MSA fee of £12,400/month and Pricing Schedule charge of £13,100/month. 05_order_form.md section 1.4; 01_msa.md section 4.1; 10_pricing.md section 1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: MSA/SOW/Order Form require monthly billing in arrears, while Pricing Schedule requires monthly billing in advance. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 05_order_form.md section 1.5; 10_pricing.md section 1.2

Payment terms conflict: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW within 45 days of receipt, and Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 05_order_form.md section 1.6

Order Form allows invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the MSA obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated payment period. 05_order_form.md sections 5.2-5.3; 01_msa.md section 4.3

Fee increase/indexation provisions conflict: MSA permits annual CPI-linked increases on 60 days' notice, while Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md section 4.4; 10_pricing.md section 1.3

Expenses provisions conflict: SOW says the Fee covers tooling, personnel and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and outside expenses need prior written approval; Pricing Schedule allows travel/subsistence at cost and requires prior approval only if expenses exceed £500/month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2-5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2

Service credit caps conflict: SOW allows credits up to 25% of monthly Fee, SLA caps them at 10%, and Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly credits at 5%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2; 10_pricing.md section 4.2
Availability commitment conflicts: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Service level start date conflicts: SOW applies service levels from Phase 3, while Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 05_order_form.md section 3.3

Support coverage conflicts: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and business-hours support for Priority 2/3, while Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md sections 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md section 3.1

Business Day is defined three different ways: MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays; Glossary uses Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2
Acceptance criteria cross-reference is broken: MSA requires assessment against Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md generally
Acceptance process conflicts: MSA requires express written acceptance, while SOW provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3

Acceptance process conflicts: Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and gives Customer 15 Business Days to assess, while SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of no response. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 5.2-5.3; 02_sow.md section 6.3

Deliverables source conflicts: SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md section 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 1.2 and 2

Deliverable definition conflicts: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while Glossary includes any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 15_glossary.md section 2
Deliverable warranty period conflicts: MSA gives a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives 180 days. 01_msa.md section 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 7.1

Change control deemed/unilateral approvals conflict with MSA requirement that any change to Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4
Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md section 4.1; 01_msa.md generally

Change Control escalation path conflicts with SOW governance escalation path: Change Control uses Delivery Lead, Programme Director, Chief Information Officer; SOW uses delivery lead, account director, executive sponsor. 08_change_control.md section 8.1; 02_sow.md section 8.3

Acceptable Use Policy permits unilateral amendment by Provider on 30 days' notice and deemed acceptance by continued use, conflicting with MSA written-change requirement and Change Control Procedure. 11_acceptable_use.md sections 8.1-8.2; 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md section 1.1

Liability caps conflict: MSA caps each party's aggregate liability at 12 months' fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2

DPA removes all liability limitations for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, directly conflicting with MSA clause 13.3 stating the MSA liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 03_dpa.md section 11.1; 01_msa.md section 13.3
Insurance requirements conflict: MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Audit rights conflict: MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/attendance rights beyond SOC 2 report, while DPA grants annual audit including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

MSA internal tension: Provider must make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights beyond SOC 2. 01_msa.md sections 12.2 and 10.2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether marked; Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or not and whether oral or written. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

Confidentiality duration may conflict with broader data/confidentiality obligations: MSA confidentiality obligations end after 3 years, while DPA/infosec treatment of personal or Customer data is not limited to 3 years and deletion/retention obligations differ. 01_msa.md section 11.3; 03_dpa.md sections 7-8; 06_infosec.md generally

Customer data retention/deletion conflicts: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, while DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Exit Plan conflicts with DPA deletion timing: Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination, while DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination. 09_exit.md section 2.3; 03_dpa.md section 8.2

Exit Plan retention is internally inconsistent with the transition period: data is retained for only 90 days after termination, but the transition period lasts until 6 months after the effective termination date and Provider must support transition throughout it. 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3
Exit Plan references DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md section 5.3; 03_dpa.md generally

Security log retention conflicts with MSA record retention: Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months, while MSA requires all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 06_infosec.md section 5.2; 01_msa.md section 12.4

Service report retention conflicts with MSA record retention: SLA retains service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, while MSA requires records to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

Data processing location restrictions conflict with SOW delivery location: DPA permits processing Customer Personal Data only in the UK/EEA, while the SOW delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 3.4

Data processing location restrictions conflict with Information Security Policy: DPA restricts processing to UK/EEA and approved locations, while the Information Security Policy allows storage/processing in any Provider region with equivalent controls as determined by Provider's CISO. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3; 06_infosec.md sections 2.1-2.3
Approved processing locations conflict: DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, while BCDR Plan uses a recovery environment in Frankfurt. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md section 3.1

Approved processing locations/subprocessors conflict: DPA Annex 2 lists London and Dublin as approved processing locations, but the Approved Subprocessor List includes Singapore processing by Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd. 03_dpa.md Annex 2 and sections 4.1-4.2; 12_subprocessors.md section 2

Subprocessor consent process conflicts: DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while Approved Subprocessor List allows additions/replacements on 30 days' notice with objection rights and even immediate replacement with notice afterwards. 03_dpa.md section 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md sections 3.1-3.4

Subcontracting consent conflicts with data-processing consent: MSA permits Provider to subcontract any Services without Customer consent, while DPA requires prior written consent for any Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but DPA Annex 2 already exists and is an Approved Processing Locations annex, not a subprocessor list. 12_subprocessors.md preamble; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or platform. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness; SLA requires 72 hours after confirmation; Information Security Policy requires 48 hours after confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3; 06_infosec.md section 6.1
SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md generally

DPA governing law is internally inconsistent: clause 13.1 applies the Agreement law except as provided in 13.2, while clause 13.2 states the whole DPA and disputes are governed by Irish law. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

DPA governing law conflicts with MSA governing law and jurisdiction: MSA applies England and Wales law and exclusive courts, while DPA applies Irish law to the DPA and disputes arising out of it. 01_msa.md sections 15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md section 13.2

AUP lawful disclosure right conflicts with confidentiality and data-processing restrictions: Provider may disclose Customer content to authorities without notice whenever it considers disclosure required, while MSA restricts disclosure of Confidential Information and DPA permits processing only on Customer's documented instructions. 11_acceptable_use.md sections 6.1-6.2; 01_msa.md section 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 2.2

Team location conflicts: SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B lists the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect as based in London. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1

Key Personnel substitution conflicts: SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified cases. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md sections 2.1-2.4

Named key personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says individuals are named in the programme initiation document, which is not included. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1.1; 02_sow.md section 3.5

SLA response-time measurement is defective: response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response deadline run from the act of responding/acknowledging rather than from Incident report or occurrence. 04_sla.md section 5.4

SLA availability formula and maintenance exclusion are internally unclear: clause 3.2 uses total minutes in the month as denominator, while clause 3.3 says maintenance windows are excluded without specifying whether they are removed from numerator, denominator, or only unavailable minutes. 04_sla.md sections 3.2-3.3

BCDR Plan suspends SLA obligations and excludes Continuity Event unavailability from availability calculations, conflicting with SLA availability/service credit regime and its listed exclusions. 07_bcdr.md sections 5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md sections 3-4 and 9

BCDR RTO can be avoided or delayed because RTO runs only from Invocation, but only Provider may declare Invocation and there is no deadline for doing so after a disruptive event. 07_bcdr.md sections 1.3, 1.5 and 4.1

BCDR Plan assumes continued availability of Provider's third-party infrastructure supplier, but also purports to cover disruptive events affecting Provider's primary production environment; this dependency may exclude a core disaster scenario without reconciling the recovery commitments. 07_bcdr.md sections 1.1-1.2 and 8.1

Information Security Policy requires Provider to classify all Customer data on receipt, while AUP says Provider does not monitor Customer content and may inspect content only on suspected breach or legal requirement. 06_infosec.md section 1.4; 11_acceptable_use.md sections 4.1-4.2

AUP permits immediate suspension for suspected policy breach, but SLA availability exclusions do not exclude Provider-imposed suspension, creating uncertainty whether suspension counts against availability and service credits while charges continue to accrue. 11_acceptable_use.md sections 5.1-5.4; 04_sla.md sections 3-4 and 9
Definition of Services conflicts: MSA limits Services to those described in a SOW, while Glossary adds support services described in the SLA. 01_msa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

Definition of Fee conflicts: MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while Glossary expands Fee to all amounts payable under the Agreement including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

Definition of Agreement conflicts: MSA defines Agreement as the MSA plus Schedules/Addenda executed under it, while Glossary includes the Order Form and every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum entered into under any of them. 01_msa.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Definition of Subprocessor conflicts: DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

Glossary definition of Personal Data as UK GDPR personal data may conflict with DPA definition of Data Protection Law as all law applicable in territories where Services are provided, especially given non-UK/EEA locations and subprocessors elsewhere. 15_glossary.md section 2; 03_dpa.md sections 1.2 and 4; 12_subprocessors.md section 2

Pricing Schedule uses 'initial term' for price freeze, but the contract has conflicting initial terms of 24 months in the MSA and 12 months in the Order Form. 10_pricing.md section 1.3; 01_msa.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 1.2

Change Control Procedure allows Provider's Delivery Lead to approve changes up to £35,000 without Customer, conflicting with Order Form commercial controls and creating unilateral charge exposure despite Customer approval requirements elsewhere. 08_change_control.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.4; 01_msa.md section 2.4

Rejected-change impact assessment charges are said to be charged at the rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but that plan states a transition assistance day rate, not a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2

Pricing standard day rate conflicts with Exit transition assistance rate: Pricing says standard out-of-scope T&M is £1,450 per person per day unless Exhibit B role rate applies, while Exit Plan charges transition assistance at £1,250 per person per day. 10_pricing.md section 2.1; 09_exit.md section 3.2

SOW states the team comprises one delivery lead, two solution architects, six engineers, one test lead and one business analyst, but Exhibit B role rates include only certain roles and identify key personnel roles differently, leaving the named/rated status of other required personnel incomplete. 02_sow.md sections 3.1-3.2; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md sections 1 and 3

SOW section 6.4 requires Provider to address Customer comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, while Exhibit A gives a defects/remediation process with a further 15 Business Day assessment period but no matching 10 Business Day remediation deadline. 02_sow.md section 6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 5.4

SOW acceptance by comments is ambiguous: it says Provider must address 'comments' and resubmit, whereas Exhibit A requires either an acceptance certificate or a written statement of defects; the standards and consequences differ. 02_sow.md section 6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 5.2-5.4

AUP prohibition on storing personal data relating to persons under 16 may conflict with the described processing of retail customer personal data, because the DPA does not exclude under-16 retail customers from the processing scope. 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.1; 03_dpa.md sections 3.2-3.3

Information Security Policy treats payment card data as Restricted Data, while AUP prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform; the contract does not reconcile whether any payment card data is permitted or prohibited. 06_infosec.md section 1.2; 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.2

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the SOW starts before the MSA Effective Date and the DPA processing location/subprocessor provisions cover services whose timing is inconsistent with the Agreement term. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 02_sow.md section 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date

Service credits are stated to be Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failure in the SLA, but DPA excludes liability limitations for data protection breaches and Security Incidents may also be Priority 1/availability events, creating conflicting remedies for the same event. 04_sla.md sections 4.3 and 7.2; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Provider's obligations during a Continuity Event are unclear because BCDR suspends SLA obligations, while Security Incidents are Priority 1 Incidents under the SLA and may also trigger DPA/InfoSec notification and assistance obligations. 07_bcdr.md section 5.1; 04_sla.md section 7.2; 03_dpa.md sections 6 and 10; 06_infosec.md section 6

Order Form ranks Addenda below Schedules, but DPA contains statutory data-processing obligations that conflict with Schedules such as the Subprocessor List and Information Security Policy; the precedence scheme would subordinate the DPA without saying whether legal compliance overrides. 05_order_form.md section 2.1; 03_dpa.md generally; 06_infosec.md section 2; 12_subprocessors.md section 3

MSA clause 13.3 says the MSA liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum, but the Order Form precedence puts the Order Form above the MSA and the DPA below Schedules, creating uncertainty whether DPA unlimited liability can ever operate. 01_msa.md section 13.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1; 05_order_form.md section 2.1

SOW says phases may overlap only where agreed in writing, but Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval and unilateral Provider approval of timetable/scope changes, which could allow phase/timetable changes without express written bilateral agreement. 02_sow.md section 4.5; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4

Maintenance notice periods use conflicting Business Day definitions, so the same 'five Business Days' notice may be calculated differently depending on whether MSA, SLA or Glossary definition applies. 04_sla.md section 3.4; 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Many operational deadlines use 'Business Days' but the contract contains conflicting definitions, affecting acceptance, incident response, reports, change control, testing, exit milestones and substitution deadlines. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2; affected schedules generally
unmatched: No clear hierarchy exists among Schedules of equal rank, yet many Schedules conflict with each other, leaving those conflicts unresolved. 05_order_form.md section 2.1(c); schedules generally

Order Form allows invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the MSA obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated payment period. 05_order_form.md sections 5.2-5.3; 01_msa.md section 4.3

Expenses provisions conflict: SOW says the Fee covers tooling, personnel and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and outside expenses need prior written approval; Pricing Schedule allows travel/subsistence at cost and requires prior approval only if expenses exceed £500/month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2-5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2

Change control deemed/unilateral approvals conflict with MSA requirement that any change to Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4

AUP lawful disclosure right conflicts with confidentiality and data-processing restrictions: Provider may disclose Customer content to authorities without notice whenever it considers disclosure required, while MSA restricts disclosure of Confidential Information and DPA permits processing only on Customer's documented instructions. 11_acceptable_use.md sections 6.1-6.2; 01_msa.md section 11.2; 03_dpa.md section 2.2

Rejected-change impact assessment charges are said to be charged at the rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but that plan states a transition assistance day rate, not a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2

SOW section 6.4 requires Provider to address Customer comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days, while Exhibit A gives a defects/remediation process with a further 15 Business Day assessment period but no matching 10 Business Day remediation deadline. 02_sow.md section 6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 5.4

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the SOW starts before the MSA Effective Date and the DPA processing location/subprocessor provisions cover services whose timing is inconsistent with the Agreement term. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 02_sow.md section 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date

findings: The document set is internally inconsistent as to precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA for conflicts. 01_msa.md section 14.2; 02_sow.md section 1.2

The Order Form creates a different precedence hierarchy and says it prevails over every other document, conflicting with the MSA precedence clause and with other documents that claim priority. 05_order_form.md section 2; 01_msa.md section 14.2

The Glossary says its definitions prevail over definitions in any other document, but the Glossary is itself Schedule 10 and is ranked below the Order Form and MSA under the Order Form precedence clause, creating circular/incompatible precedence for definitions. 15_glossary.md section 1.2; 05_order_form.md section 2.1; 01_msa.md section 14.2

The MSA definition of Agreement excludes the Order Form and Exhibits, while the Glossary definition includes the Order Form, every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum. 01_msa.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

The Agreement has conflicting initial terms: the MSA initial term is 24 months from 1 April 2027, while the Order Form initial term is 12 months from the Service Commencement Date. 01_msa.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md sections 1.2-1.3

Statement of Work 1 requires a 36-month programme, which exceeds the MSA’s 24-month initial term and the Order Form’s 12-month initial term unless renewal occurs. 02_sow.md section 2.1; 01_msa.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 1.2

Statement of Work 1 commences on 1 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027 and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 02_sow.md section 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md section 7.3

Termination notice periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days’ notice for convenience termination, while Statement of Work 1 permits termination on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md section 3.3; 02_sow.md section 2.3

Non-renewal notice under the Order Form is 30 days, while the MSA has automatic 12-month renewals unless terminated under clause 3.3, which requires 90 days’ notice. 05_order_form.md section 6; 01_msa.md sections 3.2-3.3

The recurring/monthly fee is stated inconsistently: £12,400 in the MSA, £12,800 in Statement of Work 1, £153,600 annual contract value in the Order Form implying £12,800 per month, and £13,100 in the Pricing Schedule. 01_msa.md section 4.1; 02_sow.md section 5.1; 05_order_form.md section 1.4; 10_pricing.md section 1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: the MSA, SOW and Order Form require monthly billing in arrears, while the Pricing Schedule requires monthly billing in advance. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 05_order_form.md section 1.5; 10_pricing.md section 1.2

Payment terms conflict: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, the SOW within 45 days of receipt, and the Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 05_order_form.md section 1.6

The Order Form permits invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the general obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the contractual payment period. 05_order_form.md section 5.3; 01_msa.md section 4.3

Fee increase provisions conflict: the MSA permits annual CPI-linked increases on 60 days’ notice, while the Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md section 4.4; 10_pricing.md section 1.3

Expense treatment conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and outside-Fee expenses require prior written approval, while the Pricing Schedule says travel and subsistence are recoverable at cost with approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2-5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2

Business Day is defined three different ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays, and Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Deliverable is defined differently: the MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while the Glossary includes any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 15_glossary.md section 2

Fee is defined differently: the MSA defines it as amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while the Glossary includes recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses under the whole Agreement. 01_msa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

Services are defined differently: the MSA limits Services to those described in a SOW, while the Glossary also includes support services described in the SLA Schedule. 01_msa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA requires written marking at disclosure, the DPA states all Customer Personal Data is Confidential Information whether marked or not, and the Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or oral/written. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

Security Incident is defined inconsistently across documents, ranging from unauthorised/unlawful access or loss of Customer Personal Data, to confirmed unauthorised access causing loss/corruption, to any confirmed incident affecting Customer data, to any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1; 06_infosec.md section 6.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: 24 hours from awareness under the DPA, 72 hours from confirmation under the SLA, and 48 hours from confirmation under the Information Security Policy. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3; 06_infosec.md section 6.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but Statement of Work 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Acceptance rules conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance, the SOW deems acceptance after five Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and requires a signed acceptance certificate after a 15 Business Day review period. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 5.2-5.3

Deliverables are identified inconsistently: the SOW says they are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A lists specific deliverables and says it is the sole source of acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md section 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 1.2 and 2

Acceptance review periods conflict: the SOW gives Customer five Business Days before deemed acceptance and requires resubmission within ten Business Days after comments, while Exhibit A gives Customer fifteen Business Days and then another fifteen Business Day period after resubmission. 02_sow.md sections 6.3-6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 5.2-5.4

Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA gives a 90-day conformity warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives a 180-day warranty against Material Defects. 01_msa.md section 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 7.1

Change approval procedures conflict with the MSA requirement that any change to Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation: the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval, unilateral approval by Provider’s Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4 and 6.1
The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md section 4.1; 01_msa.md

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected Change Requests at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2

Customer audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no further audit, inspection or premises/systems access beyond the SOC 2 report, while the DPA allows audits including inspection of Provider premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

MSA records access is internally unclear because Provider must make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit or inspection rights. 01_msa.md sections 12.2 and 10.2

Data retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for seven years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination, and the Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md section 2.3

The Exit Plan requires delivery of all Deliverables including source code and build scripts, while the MSA preserves Provider’s rights in pre-existing tools, methods and know-how; the documents do not distinguish what source code/build scripts are Customer-owned Deliverables versus Provider retained materials. 09_exit.md section 4.1(b); 01_msa.md sections 7.2-7.3

The Glossary defines Subprocessor as a third party processing Personal Data, while the DPA defines it as a third party processing Customer Personal Data; the broader Glossary definition may unintentionally capture Provider third parties processing non-Customer personal data. 15_glossary.md section 2; 03_dpa.md section 1.5

The Glossary defines Personal Data by reference only to the UK GDPR, while the DPA’s Data Protection Law is all applicable law in the territories where Services are provided, creating inconsistent data-protection scope if Services occur outside the UK. 15_glossary.md section 2; 03_dpa.md section 1.2

The DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the Exit Plan requires post-termination transition services and data retention, creating uncertainty whether processing may continue during the post-termination transition period. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3

The SLA requires monthly service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, conflicting with the MSA’s seven-year post-expiry/termination retention obligation for records relating to the Agreement. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4
unmatched: The Order Form permits invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the general obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the contractual payment period. 05_order_form.md section 5.3; 01_msa.md section 4.3

Expense treatment conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and outside-Fee expenses require prior written approval, while the Pricing Schedule says travel and subsistence are recoverable at cost with approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2-5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected Change Requests at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2

The SLA and SOW/Pricing documents do not provide a formula or scale for calculating the actual service credit amount, only maximum caps. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4; 10_pricing.md section 4

SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because acknowledgement is itself the response trigger. 04_sla.md section 5.4

The Information Security Policy permits Provider-controlled expansion of data regions with notice after the new region enters service, conflicting with the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation before transfers outside approved territories/locations. 06_infosec.md sections 2.1-2.3; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3

Subcontracting/subprocessing consent conflicts: the MSA allows subcontracting without prior Customer consent, the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, and the Subprocessor List allows additions/replacements on notice with only an objection right. MSA 9.3; DPA 5.1; Subprocessor List 3.1-3.4

The Subprocessor List says it is both Schedule 9 to the MSA and Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already has an Annex 2 titled Approved Processing Locations. Subprocessor List heading and preamble; DPA Annex 2

Approved processing locations conflict: the DPA limits processing to the UK/EEA and lists only London and Dublin, while the SOW uses Bengaluru, the BCDR Plan uses Frankfurt, the InfoSec Policy permits any Provider region, and the Subprocessor List includes Manchester and Singapore. DPA 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; SOW 3.4; BCDR 3.1; InfoSec Policy 2.1; Subprocessor List 2

The Singapore analytics Subprocessor conflicts with the DPA's restriction to processing only within the UK and EEA unless prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism are in place. DPA 4.1-4.2; Subprocessor List 2 and 5.1

The InfoSec Policy allows Provider to add a new processing region and notify Customer within 30 days after it enters service, conflicting with the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation for transfers outside approved territories. InfoSec Policy 2.1-2.3; DPA 4.1-4.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access beyond receiving a SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audits including premises, systems and records inspections. MSA 10.2 and 12.2; DPA 9.1-9.2

Assurance obligations conflict with the MSA's no-audit/no-inspection position, because the InfoSec Policy requires sharing penetration test reports and making the incident register available at quarterly security reviews. MSA 10.2; InfoSec Policy 6.3 and 7.2

Record and data retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for seven years, the DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination, and the Exit Plan requires retaining Customer data for 90 days after termination. MSA 12.4; DPA 8.2; Exit Plan 2.3 and 5.2

Security log retention conflicts with the MSA: the InfoSec Policy requires logs to be retained for 18 months and then deleted, while the MSA requires records, data and materials relating to the Agreement to be retained for seven years. InfoSec Policy 5.2; MSA 12.4

Service report retention conflicts or is incomplete: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records relating to the Agreement to be retained for seven years after expiry or termination. SLA 6.3; MSA 12.4

The DPA processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the Exit Plan requires Services and transition support to continue after termination and Customer data to be retained after termination, creating inconsistency for personal data processing after the Agreement ends. DPA Annex 1; Exit Plan 2.1-2.3
The Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. Exit Plan 5.3; DPA

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, the SOW caps liability at £250,000, and the DPA disapplies all limitations/exclusions for DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. MSA 13.1 and 13.3; SOW 9.2; DPA 11.1
The SOW excludes indirect or consequential loss, while the DPA says no limitation or exclusion in the Agreement applies to any breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law. SOW 9.3; DPA 11.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. MSA 16.1; SOW 9.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies the laws of England and Wales to the Agreement and disputes, while the DPA says it and disputes arising out of it are governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. MSA 15.1; DPA 13.1-13.2
The DPA's Irish governing law sits uneasily with the MSA's exclusive English and Welsh court jurisdiction, with no express jurisdiction clause for DPA disputes. MSA 15.2; DPA 13.2
The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. Change Control Procedure 4.1; MSA

Change approval rules conflict with the MSA requirement that any change to Services be agreed in writing by both parties: the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by silence, Delivery Lead approval without Customer, and emergency changes without prior approval. MSA 2.4; Change Control Procedure 4.2-4.4 and 6.1

The Change Control Procedure lets Provider's Delivery Lead approve changes costing up to £35,000 without Customer approval, conflicting with Customer payment/control obligations and the MSA's bilateral written-change requirement. Change Control Procedure 4.3; MSA 2.4 and 4

The Change Control Procedure says rejected Change Request impact assessments may be charged at the rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. Change Control Procedure 7.2; Exit Plan 3.2

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the policy on 30 days' notice with continued use deemed acceptance, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes to the Services be agreed in writing by both parties and with the Change Control Procedure. Acceptable Use Policy 8.1-8.2; MSA 2.4; Change Control Procedure 1.1

The InfoSec Policy and BCDR Plan allow material changes to be notified to Customer rather than agreed, conflicting with the MSA's bilateral written-change requirement where such changes affect the Services. InfoSec Policy 10.2; BCDR 9.3; MSA 2.4

Confidentiality and disclosure obligations conflict: the MSA permits disclosure of Confidential Information only to personnel who need to know, while the wider contract requires or permits disclosure to subcontractors, subprocessors and law enforcement/regulators. MSA 11.2; MSA 9.3; DPA 5; Subprocessor List 2; Acceptable Use Policy 6.1-6.2

The Acceptable Use Policy permits law-enforcement/regulatory disclosure without notice to Customer, while the MSA contains no legal/regulatory disclosure exception to its confidentiality restriction. Acceptable Use Policy 6.1-6.2; MSA 11.2

The BCDR Plan suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes related unavailability from availability calculations, while the SLA availability calculation excludes only agreed maintenance windows and specified customer/third-party causes. BCDR 5.1-5.3; SLA 3.1-3.3 and 9

Recovery obligations conflict with incident targets: a platform-wide outage is a Priority 1 Incident with a four-hour Resolution target, but a Continuity Event has an eight-hour RTO and SLA obligations are suspended. SLA 1.3 and 5.1; BCDR 2.1 and 5.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. SLA 7.4; DPA

The MSA requires Customer to pay all amounts without set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider, while the SLA and Pricing Schedule require service credits to be deducted from invoices. MSA 4.5; SLA 4.1; Pricing 4.1

The Order Form allows invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, which conflicts with the MSA's obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated payment period if the only issue is absence of the PO number. Order Form 5.2-5.3; MSA 4.3

The Acceptable Use Policy permits immediate suspension of the Services with charges continuing, but the SLA availability exclusions do not clearly exclude Provider-imposed suspension for alleged AUP breach, creating uncertainty over availability/service-credit consequences. Acceptable Use Policy 5.1-5.4; SLA 3 and 9

The Pricing Schedule states the recurring charge assumes up to 250,000 transactions per month and charges overages, but neither the MSA, SOW nor Order Form commercial summary identifies that volume limit or overage charging as part of the Fee/ACV. Pricing 5.1-5.2; MSA 4.1; SOW 5.1; Order Form 1.4

The Pricing Schedule says the rate card is reviewed at each anniversary of the Service Commencement Date, but 'Service Commencement Date' is defined in the Order Form and not in the MSA/Pricing Schedule itself, creating dependency on the Order Form being included despite the MSA Agreement definition issue. Pricing 7.1; Order Form 1.3; MSA 1.1

The Subprocessor List allows Provider to proceed with a new Subprocessor despite Customer's unresolved objection, while the DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to the specific Subprocessor. Subprocessor List 3.2-3.3; DPA 5.1

The Subprocessor List allows immediate Subprocessor replacement with notice afterwards for security or continuity, conflicting with the DPA requirement for prior written consent. Subprocessor List 3.4; DPA 5.1
The BCDR Plan identifies Frankfurt as the recovery environment, but Frankfurt is not listed in the DPA's approved processing locations even though data is replicated there. BCDR 3.1-3.3; DPA Annex 2

The SOW states the delivery team operates from India, but the DPA approved locations and transfer provisions do not authorise India for processing Customer Personal Data. SOW 3.4; DPA 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2
The Approved Subprocessor List includes Larkfield Support Partners in Manchester, but Manchester is not listed in the DPA's Annex 2 approved processing locations. Subprocessor List 2; DPA Annex 2

The Order Form's precedence ranks Addenda below Schedules, which could subordinate the DPA to ordinary schedules such as the SLA, InfoSec Policy and Subprocessor List even where data-protection obligations conflict. Order Form 2.1; DPA; SLA; InfoSec Policy; Subprocessor List

The SOW non-solicitation obligation applies during the programme, but the programme duration is unclear due to conflicting 12-month, 24-month and 36-month terms. SOW 9.1; MSA 3.1; SOW 2.1; Order Form 1.2

The Exit Plan requires delivery of all Deliverables including source code and build scripts, while the MSA assigns IP in Deliverables only on payment in full and Provider retains pre-existing tools, methods and know-how; the documents do not resolve what source code/build scripts are Deliverables versus Provider tools. Exit Plan 4.1(b); MSA 7.2-7.3

The Exit Plan requires Provider to deliver Customer data in the format used by Provider's systems, while the DPA requires return of Customer Personal Data in a structured, commonly used format on request. Exit Plan 4.1(a) and 5.1; DPA 8.1

The Exit Plan milestone table defines T as the effective date of termination, but the transition period begins when notice of termination is given; milestones do not address the pre-termination portion of the transition period. Exit Plan 2.1; Exit Plan Annex 1

The SLA says monthly availability is calculated across each month, while the SOW says service levels begin at Phase 3 and the Order Form says they begin on the Service Commencement Date, leaving unclear which months are measured before Phase 3. SOW 7.1; SLA 3; Order Form 3.3

findings: Conflicting order-of-precedence provisions create circular/inconsistent precedence: MSA says MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda; SOW says SOW prevails over MSA; Order Form says Order Form prevails over all and ranks Addenda below Schedules; Glossary says its definitions prevail over any other document although it is only a Schedule. 01_msa.md §§14.1-14.2; 02_sow.md §§1.1-1.2; 05_order_form.md §§2.1-2.2; 15_glossary.md §1.2
The MSA definition of Agreement excludes Order Forms and Exhibits, while the Glossary includes the Order Form, every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum. 01_msa.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

The MSA does not define or provide for an Order Form, yet Document 5 is stated to be an Order Form under the MSA and purports to form part of the agreement. 01_msa.md §§1.1, 2; 05_order_form.md heading and §2

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays; Glossary uses Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Deliverable: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified in a Statement of Work; Glossary includes any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md §1.3; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Fee: MSA limits Fee to amounts payable under MSA clause 4; Glossary includes all amounts payable, including recurring charges, time-and-materials and expenses. 01_msa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2
Conflicting definitions of Services: MSA says Services are those described in a SOW; Glossary adds support services described in the SLA. 01_msa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Confidential Information: MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure; DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether or not marked; Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement, whether marked or oral. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Security Incident: DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 15_glossary.md §2
Conflicting definitions of Subprocessor: DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data; Glossary refers to processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2
The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date, despite being issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §7.3
Conflicting commencement dates: SOW programme starts 1 March 2027, while the Order Form Service Commencement Date is 1 April 2027. 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §1.3
Conflicting initial terms: MSA initial term is 24 months; Order Form initial term is 12 months; SOW programme duration is 36 months. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2

A 36-month programme cannot be completed within either the 12-month Order Form initial term or the 24-month MSA initial term unless renewals occur, but the documents do not reconcile this dependency. 01_msa.md §§3.1-3.2; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §§1.2, 6.1

Conflicting termination/non-renewal notice periods: MSA convenience termination requires 90 days; SOW convenience termination requires 30 days; Order Form non-renewal requires 30 days. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3; 05_order_form.md §6.2

MSA automatic renewal is avoided only by termination under clause 3.3, while the Order Form creates a separate non-renewal mechanism with different notice. 01_msa.md §§3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md §§6.1-6.2

Conflicting monthly charges: MSA states £12,400; SOW states £12,800; Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 implies £12,800 per month; Pricing Schedule states £13,100 per month. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Conflicting invoicing timing: MSA, SOW and Order Form require monthly billing in arrears; Pricing Schedule requires monthly billing in advance on the first Business Day of each month. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.5; 10_pricing.md §§1.2, 6.1

Conflicting payment terms: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt; SOW requires 45 days of receipt; Order Form requires 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Conflicting price-increase rules: MSA permits annual CPI increases on 60 days' notice; Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge for the initial term and bars indexation or increases during that period. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Conflicting expenses rules: SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and requires prior approval for expenses outside the Fee; Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires approval only if expenses exceed £500 in a month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Conflicting rate cards for time-and-materials work: Pricing Schedule standard rate is £1,450 per person per day for every role unless Exhibit B applies, while Exhibit B sets lower role-specific rates for Engineers, Test Leads and Business Analysts. 10_pricing.md §§2.1, 2.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3

Transition assistance rate of £1,250 per person per day conflicts with the Pricing Schedule standard rate of £1,450 and Exhibit B role rates, with no precedence or carve-out specific to exit assistance. 09_exit.md §3.2; 10_pricing.md §2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3

Change Control Procedure refers to the rate for rejected-change impact assessments being set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not set a rate for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

MSA requires any change to Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, but Change Control permits deemed approval by silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead for changes up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §§4.2-4.4, 6.1

Provider's Delivery Lead may approve changes with a cost impact up to £35,000 without Customer approval, which conflicts with Customer's payment obligations and the MSA requirement for written agreement by both parties. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §4.3
Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md §4.1; 01_msa.md

Acceptable Use Policy permits Provider to amend the policy unilaterally on 30 days' notice, with acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes to Services be agreed in writing by both parties. 01_msa.md §2.4; 11_acceptable_use.md §§8.1-8.2
MSA acceptance clause refers to Schedule 1, Section 12 for acceptance criteria, but SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Conflicting acceptance mechanisms: MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly confirms acceptance in writing; SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence; Exhibit A requires a signed acceptance certificate and says silence does not constitute acceptance. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§5.2-5.3

Conflicting acceptance review periods: SOW gives Customer 5 Business Days before deemed acceptance; Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days to assess. 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.2

Conflicting resubmission/remediation periods for rejected Deliverables: SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments; Exhibit A gives a new 15-Business-Day assessment cycle after remedy and resubmission without the same 10-day remedy deadline. 02_sow.md §6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.4

Conflicting sources of Deliverables and acceptance criteria: SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead; Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2, 3

Key acceptance inputs are missing or external to the contract set: requirements register, agreed functional test pack, phase plan, and programme initiation document are referenced but not included. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1
Conflicting Deliverable warranty periods: MSA warranty is 90 days after acceptance; Exhibit A warranty is 180 days after acceptance. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Customer must nominate a single point of contact under the MSA, but the Order Form names separate commercial and technical contacts and other documents refer to different nominated contacts/security contacts without identifying one single point of contact. 01_msa.md §5.2; 05_order_form.md §§4.1-4.2; 03_dpa.md §6.3; 04_sla.md §7.3; 07_bcdr.md §4.2
SLA refers to Customer's nominated security contact, but no nominated security contact is identified in the Order Form or elsewhere in the contract set. 04_sla.md §7.3; 05_order_form.md §4
SLA states Security Incident escalation contacts are listed in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md
Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md
DPA Annex 2 is approved processing locations, but the Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, creating two inconsistent Annex 2s. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md heading

Approved Subprocessor List contains Singapore processing by Kestrel Analytics, conflicting with DPA restrictions to the UK/EEA and DPA Annex 2 locations of London and Dublin only. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md §2

SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, which conflicts with DPA restrictions that Customer Personal Data be processed only in the UK/EEA and approved locations of London and Dublin. 02_sow.md §3.4; 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

BCDR Plan states the recovery environment is in Frankfurt, Germany, while DPA Annex 2 identifies Dublin, Ireland as the disaster recovery location and does not list Frankfurt. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md §3.1

Information Security Policy permits Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region with equivalent controls, determined by Provider's CISO, conflicting with DPA's UK/EEA-only and Annex 2 location restrictions and prior authorisation requirement for transfers. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3; 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3
MSA allows Provider to subcontract any Services without Customer consent, while DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

Approved Subprocessor List permits adding/replacing subprocessors on 30 days' notice with an objection process, and emergency replacement with notice afterwards, conflicting with DPA requirement for Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

Approved Subprocessor List permits Provider to proceed with a new Subprocessor despite Customer's unresolved objection, conflicting with DPA's specific prior written consent requirement. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §3.3

Conflicting audit rights: MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/right to attend Provider premises or systems beyond annual SOC 2 report; DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records; Information Security Policy gives access to penetration test reports and incident registers. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.3; 06_infosec.md §§6.3, 7.2

MSA record-access clause requires Provider to make records available on request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit, inspection or attendance rights, making the record-access right internally inconsistent. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Conflicting record/data retention and deletion duties: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination; DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days; Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination; Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months; SLA retains service reports only for the Agreement duration. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2; 06_infosec.md §5.2; 04_sla.md §6.3

Exit transition obligations require Services to continue throughout a transition period ending six months after termination, while DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of expiry or termination, which may prevent continued service/transition performance. 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but Exit Plan requires post-termination transition assistance and Customer data retention, creating uncertainty over lawful processing during transition. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

Conflicting liability caps/exclusions: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000; DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2; 03_dpa.md §11.1
SOW exclusion of indirect/consequential loss conflicts with DPA clause stating no exclusion of liability applies to breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance requirements: MSA requires at least £5,000,000 aggregate cover; SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Conflicting governing law: MSA provides England and Wales law and exclusive courts; DPA internally says it is governed by Agreement law except clause 13.2, then clause 13.2 says Irish law governs the DPA and disputes arising out of it. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

DPA clause 13.1 and 13.2 are internally inconsistent because 13.1 adopts the Agreement law except as provided in 13.2, while 13.2 replaces it entirely with Irish law for the DPA and disputes. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2
Conflicting availability commitments: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability; SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability. 02_sow.md §7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Conflicting start date for service levels: SOW says platform service levels apply from the start of Phase 3; Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md §7.1; 05_order_form.md §3.3

Conflicting support coverage: SLA provides 24x7 only for Priority 1 and Business-Day 08:00-18:00 support for Priority 2/3; Order Form says 24x7 for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

Conflicting service credit caps: SOW permits credits up to 25% of monthly Fee; SLA caps monthly credits at 10%; Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly credits at 5%. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2; 10_pricing.md §4.2
SOW provides service credits for availability failures but does not state how credits are calculated within the 'up to 25%' cap. 02_sow.md §7.4

SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for failure to meet availability, which may conflict with DPA's no-limitation/no-exclusion wording if an availability failure is also a data protection/security breach and with MSA/DPA liability provisions generally. 04_sla.md §4.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1; 01_msa.md §13

BCDR suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes resulting unavailability from availability calculations, while SLA availability provisions do not include Continuity Events as an exclusion other than agreed maintenance/other listed exclusions. 04_sla.md §§3.1-3.3, 9; 07_bcdr.md §§5.1-5.3

BCDR RTO is 8 hours from Invocation, but SLA Priority 1 Resolution target is 4 hours; a primary production outage may satisfy one provision while breaching the other unless the BCDR suspension applies, creating inconsistent operational targets. 04_sla.md §5.1; 07_bcdr.md §§1.2, 2.1, 5.1

SLA response and resolution times are measured only from Provider's acknowledgement in its tool, not from incident occurrence or Customer report, allowing Provider to delay acknowledgement and making targets internally defective. 04_sla.md §5.4

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines and triggers: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness; Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation; SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming a narrower category of Security Incident. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 06_infosec.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3

SLA treats a Security Incident as Priority 1 requiring 15-minute response and 4-hour Resolution, but its notification deadline is 72 hours after confirmation, creating inconsistent urgency obligations. 04_sla.md §§5.1, 7.2-7.3

DPA prohibits public statements about Security Incidents without Customer approval, while Acceptable Use Policy allows disclosure of Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without any obligation to notify Customer; the interaction is unresolved where a disclosure relates to Customer Personal Data or an incident. 03_dpa.md §6.3; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2

Acceptable Use Policy says Provider does not monitor Customer content, while Information Security Policy requires Provider to classify all Customer data on receipt as Restricted or Internal, which may require inspection/monitoring. 11_acceptable_use.md §4.1; 06_infosec.md §1.4

Acceptable Use Policy permits immediate suspension for suspected breach with charges continuing, but SLA availability exclusions do not expressly exclude AUP suspensions, creating potential simultaneous obligation to provide availability and right not to provide service. 11_acceptable_use.md §§5.1-5.4; 04_sla.md §§3, 9

Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, while Information Security Policy includes payment card data within Restricted Data and imposes controls for it, creating inconsistent assumptions about whether such data may exist on the platform. 11_acceptable_use.md §3.2; 06_infosec.md §1.2

SOW states the entire delivery team operates from Bengaluru, but Exhibit B lists key personnel base locations in London and Bengaluru, including Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Conflicting key-personnel substitution rules: SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement; Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1-2.4

SOW refers to named key personnel, but the names are not included in the contract set and are said to be in a programme initiation document that is not provided. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1

SOW requires a team of at least 11 FTE with two solution architects, six engineers, one test lead and one business analyst, while Exhibit B identifies only four Key Personnel; it is unclear which personnel are key and subject to substitution restrictions. 02_sow.md §§3.1-3.2; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Order Form support contact is Provider's service desk, while SOW escalation begins with the Delivery Lead and Order Form separately names Provider delivery and commercial contacts; support/escalation responsibility is unclear. 05_order_form.md §§3.2, 4.3-4.4; 02_sow.md §8.3

Change Control escalation path differs from the SOW governance escalation path and uses roles not otherwise defined in the governance structure, creating inconsistent escalation routes. 02_sow.md §8.3; 08_change_control.md §8.1

Pricing Schedule uses Service Commencement Date for annual rate-card review, but Service Commencement Date is defined only in the Order Form, which the MSA does not incorporate in its definition of Agreement. 05_order_form.md §1.3; 10_pricing.md §7.1; 01_msa.md §1.1

DPA states Annex 1 sets out processing details 'in full', but the contract set adds additional processing locations/subprocessors and operational processing not reflected in Annex 1 or Annex 2. 03_dpa.md §§3.4, 4.3 and Annexes 1-2; 02_sow.md §3.4; 07_bcdr.md §3.1; 12_subprocessors.md §2

Subprocessor list is maintained and published by Provider on its trust portal, but DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; a Provider-maintained current list may change without forming an executed amendment. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§1.2, 3

DPA requires processing only on Customer's documented instructions, while AUP permits Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement/regulators whenever Provider considers it required, without Customer notice; the documents do not reconcile this with controller instructions for personal data. 03_dpa.md §2.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2

Exit Plan requires delivery of all Deliverables including source code and build scripts, while MSA lets Provider retain pre-existing tools, methods and know-how; the documents do not distinguish deliverable source code from Provider tools or pre-existing code. 01_msa.md §§7.2-7.3; 09_exit.md §4.1(b)

Exit Plan requires Provider to deliver all Customer data in the format used by Provider's systems, while DPA requires return of Customer Personal Data in a structured, commonly used format on request; formats may not match. 03_dpa.md §8.1; 09_exit.md §4.1(a)

Exit Plan milestone dates are measured from effective termination, but the transition period begins when notice of termination is given and continues six months after effective termination; milestones before/after termination are not tied to the actual transition start date. 09_exit.md §§2.1, 7.1 and Annex 1

Order Form allows invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, while MSA requires payment of undisputed invoices within 30 days of receipt; the documents do not state whether a missing PO makes an otherwise undisputed invoice disputable. 01_msa.md §4.3; 05_order_form.md §§5.2-5.3

Pricing Schedule requires invoice queries within 10 Business Days of receipt, but MSA payment obligation applies to undisputed invoices without any dispute deadline; the effect of late invoice disputes is unclear. 01_msa.md §4.3; 10_pricing.md §6.3
unmatched: The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date, despite being issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §7.3

MSA automatic renewal is avoided only by termination under clause 3.3, while the Order Form creates a separate non-renewal mechanism with different notice. 01_msa.md §§3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md §§6.1-6.2

Conflicting expenses rules: SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and requires prior approval for expenses outside the Fee; Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires approval only if expenses exceed £500 in a month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Change Control Procedure refers to the rate for rejected-change impact assessments being set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not set a rate for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

Conflicting resubmission/remediation periods for rejected Deliverables: SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments; Exhibit A gives a new 15-Business-Day assessment cycle after remedy and resubmission without the same 10-day remedy deadline. 02_sow.md §6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.4

Key acceptance inputs are missing or external to the contract set: requirements register, agreed functional test pack, phase plan, and programme initiation document are referenced but not included. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1

Customer must nominate a single point of contact under the MSA, but the Order Form names separate commercial and technical contacts and other documents refer to different nominated contacts/security contacts without identifying one single point of contact. 01_msa.md §5.2; 05_order_form.md §§4.1-4.2; 03_dpa.md §6.3; 04_sla.md §7.3; 07_bcdr.md §4.2
SLA refers to Customer's nominated security contact, but no nominated security contact is identified in the Order Form or elsewhere in the contract set. 04_sla.md §7.3; 05_order_form.md §4

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but Exit Plan requires post-termination transition assistance and Customer data retention, creating uncertainty over lawful processing during transition. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3
SOW exclusion of indirect/consequential loss conflicts with DPA clause stating no exclusion of liability applies to breach of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 02_sow.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1

DPA clause 13.1 and 13.2 are internally inconsistent because 13.1 adopts the Agreement law except as provided in 13.2, while 13.2 replaces it entirely with Irish law for the DPA and disputes. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

SLA response and resolution times are measured only from Provider's acknowledgement in its tool, not from incident occurrence or Customer report, allowing Provider to delay acknowledgement and making targets internally defective. 04_sla.md §5.4

SOW refers to named key personnel, but the names are not included in the contract set and are said to be in a programme initiation document that is not provided. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1

Order Form support contact is Provider's service desk, while SOW escalation begins with the Delivery Lead and Order Form separately names Provider delivery and commercial contacts; support/escalation responsibility is unclear. 05_order_form.md §§3.2, 4.3-4.4; 02_sow.md §8.3

Change Control escalation path differs from the SOW governance escalation path and uses roles not otherwise defined in the governance structure, creating inconsistent escalation routes. 02_sow.md §8.3; 08_change_control.md §8.1

Exit Plan milestone dates are measured from effective termination, but the transition period begins when notice of termination is given and continues six months after effective termination; milestones before/after termination are not tied to the actual transition start date. 09_exit.md §§2.1, 7.1 and Annex 1
