Expense recovery provisions conflict: the SOW says the Fee covers travel and tooling unless expressly stated otherwise and requires prior written approval for expenses outside the Fee; the Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only where expenses exceed £500 per month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2 and 5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2

The Change Control Procedure refers to charging for rejected-change impact assessments at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan contains no rate for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2
The MSA requires Customer to assess Deliverables against Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12. 01_msa.md section 6.2; 02_sow.md

Acceptance rules conflict: the MSA requires express written acceptance, the SOW provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and a signed acceptance certificate is required. 01_msa.md section 6.1; 02_sow.md section 6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 5.2-5.3

Acceptance review periods conflict: the SOW gives Customer 5 Business Days before deemed acceptance, while Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days to accept or issue defects. 02_sow.md section 6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 5.2

Deliverable sources conflict: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md section 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 1.2 and 2
Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA gives a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives a 180-day warranty. 01_msa.md section 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 7.1

The definition of Deliverable conflicts: the MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while the Glossary defines Deliverable as any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md section 1.3; 15_glossary.md definition of Deliverable

The definition of Fee conflicts: the MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under clause 4, while the Glossary expands it to all amounts payable under the Agreement, including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md definition of Fee

The definition of Services conflicts: the MSA defines Services as those described in a SOW, while the Glossary also includes support services described in the SLA Schedule. 01_msa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md definition of Services

The definition of Business Day conflicts across the documents: the MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; the SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays; the Glossary uses Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md section 1.2; 04_sla.md section 1.1; 15_glossary.md definition of Business Day

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, the DPA treats all Customer Personal Data as Confidential Information whether marked or not, and the Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked, oral or written. 01_msa.md section 11.1; 03_dpa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md definition of Confidential Information

The liability regime conflicts: the MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, the SOW caps liability at £250,000, and the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Insurance requirements conflict: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Subcontracting/subprocessor approval rights conflict: the MSA permits Provider to subcontract without prior Customer consent; the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor; the Approved Subprocessor List allows additions/replacements on notice and even allows Provider to proceed after unresolved objection or replace immediately in urgent cases. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md sections 3.1-3.4

Data processing locations conflict: the DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin as approved locations, while the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, and the Information Security Policy allows processing in any Provider region determined by Provider's CISO. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md section 3.4; 06_infosec.md sections 2.1-2.3
The BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt is not listed as an approved processing location in the DPA, which lists only London and Dublin. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md section 3.1

The Approved Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, which conflicts with the DPA restriction to processing within the UK and EEA unless prior written authorisation and a transfer mechanism are in place. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.2; 12_subprocessors.md section 2

The Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already has an Annex 2 titled Approved Processing Locations. This creates two inconsistent Annex 2s. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md heading and preamble

The Approved Subprocessor List contains subprocessor locations, including Manchester and Singapore, that are not the approved processing locations listed in the DPA Annex 2. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md section 2

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: the DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption; the Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1; 15_glossary.md definition of Security Incident

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation, and the Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3; 06_infosec.md section 6.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

Record/data retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination; the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination; the Exit Plan requires retention of all Customer data for 90 days after termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md section 2.3

The Exit Plan requires Provider to support a transition period ending 6 months after termination, but also requires retention of Customer data for only 90 days after termination, potentially requiring deletion before the transition period ends. 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3 and 5.2

The DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days of expiry/termination, which is incompatible with the Exit Plan's requirement that Provider continue services and provide data-dependent transition assistance for up to 6 months after termination. 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3 and 4.1
The Exit Plan refers to Provider's personal-data obligations being set out in DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md section 5.3; 03_dpa.md

Security log retention conflicts with the MSA's general retention period: the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be retained for 18 months and then deleted, while the MSA requires all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 06_infosec.md section 5.2; 01_msa.md section 12.4

Service report retention conflicts with the MSA's general retention period: the SLA requires reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement, while the MSA requires records to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

Availability commitments conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability and the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 3.3

Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows service credits of up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps credits at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly credits at 5%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2; 10_pricing.md section 4.2

The SLA says service credits are the sole financial remedy for availability failure, which conflicts with broader remedies and liability positions in the MSA and DPA, especially the DPA's statement that no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 04_sla.md section 4.3; 01_msa.md section 13; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and limits Priority 2/3 support to 08:00-18:00 on Business Days, while the Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md sections 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md section 3.1

SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making response-time obligations circular and allowing Provider to delay acknowledgement before the clock starts. 04_sla.md section 5.4

BCDR recovery obligations conflict with ordinary SLA obligations: a platform-wide outage would be Priority 1 with a 4-hour resolution target, but the BCDR Plan sets an 8-hour RTO and suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event. 04_sla.md sections 1.3 and 5.1; 07_bcdr.md sections 2.1 and 5.1

The BCDR Plan excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations, while the SLA availability exclusions are limited to agreed maintenance windows, Customer network/equipment, and certain third-party services. 04_sla.md sections 3.2-3.3 and 9; 07_bcdr.md section 5.3

The BCDR Plan allows up to 12 hours of planned unavailability for return to the primary environment without expressly requiring the SLA's 5 Business Days' notice for maintenance windows. 04_sla.md section 3.4; 07_bcdr.md section 5.2

Key personnel location commitments conflict: the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London and only two key roles in Bengaluru. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1

Key personnel substitution rights conflict: the SOW prohibits substituting named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md sections 2.1 and 2.4

Exhibit B refers to named individuals in the programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set, leaving the named Key Personnel unidentified. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1.1

Change approval rules conflict with the MSA's requirement that any change be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation: the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead for changes up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4 and 6.1

The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17 and does not describe a Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md section 4.1; 01_msa.md

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the policy on 30 days' notice with acceptance by continued use, which conflicts with the MSA requirement that changes to the Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation and the Change Control Procedure's formal change process. 11_acceptable_use.md sections 8.1-8.2; 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md section 1.1

Governing law is internally inconsistent in the DPA: clause 13.1 applies the law applicable to the Agreement, but clause 13.2 says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. This also conflicts with the MSA's England and Wales governing law. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2; 01_msa.md section 15.1

The DPA changes governing law to Ireland but does not address jurisdiction, while the MSA gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales, creating uncertainty for DPA disputes. 03_dpa.md section 13; 01_msa.md section 15.2

The definition of Subprocessor conflicts: the DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md definition of Subprocessor

The DPA definition of Data Protection Law depends on the territories in which Services are provided; because the SOW says the delivery team operates from India while the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA, the applicable data-protection-law scope is uncertain. 03_dpa.md sections 1.2 and 4.1; 02_sow.md section 3.4
The DPA Annex 1 data categories use 'loyalty identifiers' while the DPA body uses 'loyalty scheme identifiers', creating minor terminology inconsistency. 03_dpa.md section 3.3 and Annex 1
The SOW's service credit entitlement of 'up to' 25% does not state how the credit is calculated, making the remedy incomplete/uncertain. 02_sow.md section 7.4
The SLA states a monthly service credit applies for availability failures but provides only a cap, not a calculation or scale for the actual credit amount. 04_sla.md sections 4.1-4.2

The MSA requires Customer to nominate a single point of contact, while the Order Form names multiple Customer contacts and the SLA refers to a separate nominated security contact that is not identified. 01_msa.md section 5.2; 05_order_form.md sections 4.1-4.2; 04_sla.md section 7.3

The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storage of personal data relating to persons under 16, while the DPA processing scope includes Customer retail customers without any age limitation; for a retail customer platform these obligations may be incompatible unless under-16 customer data is excluded operationally. 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.1; 03_dpa.md sections 3.2 and Annex 1

The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, while the Information Security Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data and imposes controls for it, creating ambiguity as to whether payment card data is permitted if secured or prohibited entirely. 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.2; 06_infosec.md section 1.2

The Pricing Schedule refers to 'Exhibit B' for role-specific rates; Exhibit B is an exhibit to the SOW, not expressly to the Pricing Schedule, creating an incorporation/reference ambiguity. 10_pricing.md section 2.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md heading and section 3

The SOW says the delivery team comprises specific roles but Exhibit B's role rates include Engineers and Business Analyst without key-personnel treatment, while Exhibit B key-personnel commitments identify only four roles; this is not fatal but leaves the identity and commitment of the remaining seven FTEs less certain. 02_sow.md sections 3.1-3.2; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md sections 1 and 4

The MSA's audit clause requires Provider to furnish an annual SOC 2 Type II report, but no timing, period covered, or fallback is stated if Provider does not have such a report. 01_msa.md section 10.2

The Exit Plan requires delivery of 'all Deliverables, including source code and build scripts', but the MSA assigns IP in Deliverables only on payment in full and Provider retains pre-existing tools, methods and know-how; the Exit Plan does not distinguish Provider pre-existing materials from Customer-owned Deliverables. 09_exit.md section 4.1(b); 01_msa.md sections 7.2-7.3

findings: Circular/inconsistent order of precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda, the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says the Order Form prevails over all other documents and ranks Addenda below Schedules, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over any other definition despite being only a Schedule under the Order Form ranking. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md clause 1.2; 05_order_form.md clauses 2.1-2.2; 15_glossary.md clause 1.2

The Order Form is not clearly incorporated by the MSA definition of Agreement, which includes the MSA, Schedules and Addenda but not order forms; the Order Form nevertheless purports to form and rank the agreement documents. 01_msa.md clause 1.1; 05_order_form.md clause 2
Conflicting initial terms: MSA initial term is 24 months, SOW programme is 36 months, and Order Form initial term is 12 months. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 02_sow.md clause 2.1; 05_order_form.md clause 1.2
SOW programme commences before the MSA Effective Date and before the Order Form signature date. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md clause 2.2; 05_order_form.md clause 7.3

Conflicting termination/non-renewal notice periods: MSA convenience termination requires 90 days, SOW convenience termination requires 30 days, and Order Form non-renewal requires 30 days. 01_msa.md clause 3.3; 02_sow.md clause 2.3; 05_order_form.md clause 6.2

Conflicting monthly recurring charges: MSA states £12,400, SOW states £12,800, Pricing Schedule states £13,100, while Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 implies £12,800 per month. 01_msa.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md clause 5.1; 05_order_form.md clauses 1.4-1.5; 10_pricing.md clause 1.1

Conflicting invoicing timing: MSA, SOW and Order Form require monthly invoicing in arrears, while Pricing Schedule requires monthly invoicing in advance on the first Business Day of each month. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3; 05_order_form.md clause 1.5; 10_pricing.md clauses 1.2 and 6.1

Conflicting payment periods: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW within 45 days of receipt, and Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3; 05_order_form.md clause 1.6

Conflicting charge-increase/indexation provisions: MSA permits CPI-linked increases once per 12 months on 60 days' notice, while Pricing Schedule says recurring charges are fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md clause 4.4; 10_pricing.md clause 1.3

Conflicting expense treatment: SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval; Pricing Schedule makes travel/subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md clauses 5.2 and 5.4; 10_pricing.md clauses 3.1-3.2
Conflicting definitions of Business Day across the contract set. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting definitions of Agreement: MSA excludes the Order Form and Exhibits unless they are Schedules/Addenda, while Glossary expressly includes the Order Form, every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum. 01_msa.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting definitions of Deliverable: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, SOW says Deliverables are in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, Exhibit A lists specific Deliverables and says it is the sole source, and Glossary expands Deliverables to any output of Services. 01_msa.md clause 1.3; 02_sow.md clause 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 1.2 and 2; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting definitions of Fee: MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while Glossary defines Fee as all amounts payable under the Agreement including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md clause 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting definitions of Services: MSA limits Services to those described in a SOW, while Glossary adds support services described in the Service Level and Support Schedule. 01_msa.md clause 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting definitions of Confidential Information: MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing, DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether marked or not, and Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or oral/written. 01_msa.md clause 11.1; 03_dpa.md clause 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

MSA confidentiality obligations expire after 3 years, while records/data retention obligations extend longer; confidential records could be retained after confidentiality protection expires. 01_msa.md clause 11.3; 01_msa.md clause 12.4
MSA acceptance cross-reference is wrong: it refers to Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md

Conflicting acceptance mechanics: MSA requires express written acceptance, SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days' silence, and Exhibit A requires a signed acceptance certificate and states silence does not constitute acceptance. 01_msa.md clause 6.1; 02_sow.md clause 6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 5.2-5.3

Conflicting acceptance review periods: SOW allows 5 Business Days before deemed acceptance and 10 Business Days to resubmit after comments, while Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days for assessment and a further 15 Business Day period after resubmission. 02_sow.md clauses 6.3-6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 5.2 and 5.4
Conflicting warranty periods for accepted Deliverables: MSA warranty is 90 days; Exhibit A warranty is 180 days. 01_msa.md clause 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clause 7.1

Conflicting liability caps: MSA caps each party at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps Provider at £250,000; DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md clause 9.2; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1

DPA indemnity for fines may conflict with the SOW exclusion of indirect/consequential loss and the MSA liability cap, with no coherent precedence due to conflicting precedence clauses. 02_sow.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 11.2; 01_msa.md clause 13
Conflicting professional indemnity insurance limits: MSA requires at least £5,000,000; SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md clause 9.4

Conflicting audit rights: MSA/SOC 2 clause gives Customer no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises/systems, while DPA allows audits including premises, systems and records, and Information Security Policy requires sharing penetration test reports and making incident registers available. 01_msa.md clause 10.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 9.1-9.2; 06_infosec.md clauses 6.3 and 7.2

MSA records access is circularly limited by the no-audit clause: records must be made available on request only in accordance with clause 10.2, which says Customer has no further audit/inspection rights. 01_msa.md clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessor consent: MSA allows subcontracting without Customer consent, DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, and the Approved Subprocessor List allows additions/replacements on notice and even allows Provider to proceed after objection. 01_msa.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md clauses 3.1-3.4

Data processing location conflict: DPA restricts Customer Personal Data to the UK/EEA and Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, while SOW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India and Exhibit B places key personnel in Bengaluru. 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md clause 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1

Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored/processed in any Provider region chosen by Provider's CISO with notice only after a new region enters service, conflicting with DPA restrictions requiring UK/EEA processing, approved locations and prior written authorisation for transfers. 06_infosec.md clauses 2.1-2.3; 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1-4.3
BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt is not listed as an approved processing location in DPA Annex 2, despite replicated data being sent there. 07_bcdr.md clauses 3.1-3.3; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Approved Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, conflicting with DPA's UK/EEA-only processing restriction and approved locations of London and Dublin unless separately authorised. 12_subprocessors.md section 2; 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already has an Annex 2 containing approved processing locations, not subprocessors. 12_subprocessors.md preamble; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Conflicting Security Incident definitions: DPA uses a broad unauthorised/unlawful access/acquisition/alteration/disclosure/loss/destruction definition for Customer Personal Data, SLA uses only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption, and Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md clause 1.6; 04_sla.md clause 7.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines and triggers: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, Information Security Policy within 48 hours of confirmation, and SLA within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 06_infosec.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3
SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md clause 7.4; 03_dpa.md

DPA governing law is internally inconsistent and conflicts with MSA: clause 13.1 points to the Agreement law, while clause 13.2 says the DPA and disputes are governed by Irish law; MSA uses England and Wales law and exclusive courts. 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1-13.2; 01_msa.md clauses 15.1-15.2
Conflicting availability commitments: SOW requires 99.5%, SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md clause 7.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.1

Conflicting start date for service levels: SOW applies service levels from Phase 3, while Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md clause 7.1; 05_order_form.md clause 3.3

Conflicting service credit caps: SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, SLA caps at 10%, and Pricing Schedule caps aggregate service credits at 5% of the recurring monthly charge. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clause 4.2; 10_pricing.md clause 4.2

Conflicting service credit process/remedy: SLA says credits are applied automatically and are the sole financial remedy for availability failure; Pricing Schedule applies credits against recurring invoices and imposes a lower aggregate cap; SOW states a separate entitlement up to 25% without saying it is sole remedy or automatic. 04_sla.md clauses 4.1-4.3; 10_pricing.md clauses 4.1-4.3; 02_sow.md clause 7.4

Conflicting support coverage: SLA provides 24/7 support only for Priority 1 and business-hours support for Priority 2/3, while Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md clauses 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md clause 3.1

SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time obligation circular because acknowledgement is itself the response trigger. 04_sla.md clause 5.4

BCDR suspends SLA obligations and excludes Continuity Event unavailability and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations, conflicting with the SLA availability regime and its stated exclusions. 07_bcdr.md clauses 5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md clauses 3.2-3.3 and 9

BCDR RTO is 8 hours from Provider's Invocation, while SLA Priority 1 Resolution target is 4 hours; a major outage could be subject to incompatible restoration targets depending on classification. 07_bcdr.md clause 2.1; 04_sla.md clause 5.1

BCDR RTO runs only from Provider's formal Invocation and only Provider's Head of Operations may invoke, so Provider can delay the start of the RTO clock; this undermines the stated recovery objective. 07_bcdr.md clauses 1.5, 2.1 and 4.1

Conflicting data retention/deletion obligations: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination; DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination; Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination and deletion only after retention and handover. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 03_dpa.md clauses 8.2-8.3; 09_exit.md clauses 2.3 and 5.2
Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md clause 5.3; 03_dpa.md

Sources of Deliverables and acceptance criteria conflict: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md section 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md sections 1.2 and 2
The Deliverables phase plan referenced in the SOW is not included in the contract set, making the contractual Deliverables uncertain unless Exhibit A overrides it. 02_sow.md section 6.1

Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA gives a 90-day conformity warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives a 180-day warranty against Material Defects. 01_msa.md section 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md section 7.1

Provider team location conflicts: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1

Key Personnel substitution rules conflict: the SOW requires Customer’s prior written agreement, while Exhibit B permits substitution on ten Business Days’ notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 2

Named Key Personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says they are named in a programme initiation document, which is not supplied. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1.1

Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1, while the Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md sections 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md section 3.1

Service level start date conflicts: the SOW says platform service levels apply from the start of Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md section 7.1; 05_order_form.md section 3.3
Availability target conflicts: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md section 7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1

Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps them at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps all service credits at 5%. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2; 10_pricing.md section 4.2

Service credit mechanics conflict: the SLA requires Provider to apply credits automatically without a claim, while the SOW only states Customer is entitled to credits of up to 25% and does not state automatic application. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.1

The SLA makes service credits the sole financial remedy for availability failure, which may conflict with broader remedies and liability provisions elsewhere, including the DPA’s unlimited liability for data protection breaches if an availability failure is also a data/security incident. 04_sla.md section 4.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1; 01_msa.md section 13

SLA response and resolution targets are measured from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, which makes the response-time obligation circular or ineffective because acknowledgement is itself the response trigger. 04_sla.md section 5.4

Security Incident definitions conflict: the DPA covers any unauthorised or unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption; the Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1; 15_glossary.md section 2

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation, and the Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md section 6.1; 04_sla.md section 7.3; 06_infosec.md section 6.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md section 7.4; 03_dpa.md

Processing location obligations conflict: the DPA permits processing only in the UK and EEA and lists London/Dublin as approved locations, while the SOW delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, and the Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored or processed in any Provider region selected by Provider’s CISO. 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md section 3.4; 06_infosec.md section 2.1
The BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt is not listed in the DPA’s approved processing locations, which list only London and Dublin. 07_bcdr.md section 3.1; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

The Approved Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics in Singapore, conflicting with the DPA restriction that Customer Personal Data be processed only in the UK and EEA absent prior written authorisation. 12_subprocessors.md section 2; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.2

The Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA’s Annex 2 is already titled “Approved Processing Locations” and lists locations, not subprocessors. 12_subprocessors.md preamble; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Subprocessor approval mechanisms conflict: the DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Approved Subprocessor List allows Provider to add or replace subprocessors on notice, with only an objection right, and in some cases immediate replacement with notice afterwards. 03_dpa.md section 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md sections 3.1-3.4

General subcontracting rights conflict with data-processing restrictions: the MSA allows subcontracting any part of the Services without prior consent, while the DPA requires prior consent for any Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access beyond the SOC 2 report, while the DPA gives Customer annual audit rights including inspection of Provider premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

MSA records access is internally inconsistent because Provider must make records available on request “in accordance with clause 10.2”, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit or inspection right beyond receiving the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Record and data retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for seven years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination and the Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md section 2.3

Security log retention conflicts with the MSA’s seven-year retention obligation: the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be retained for 18 months and then deleted. 06_infosec.md section 5.2; 01_msa.md section 12.4

Service report retention conflicts with the MSA’s seven-year retention obligation: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement. 04_sla.md section 6.3; 01_msa.md section 12.4

The Exit Plan’s 90-day post-termination data retention conflicts internally with its six-month post-termination transition period because data may need to be retained to support the full transition period. 09_exit.md sections 2.1 and 2.3

The Exit Plan requires Provider to continue providing Services during the transition period after termination, but the DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days of termination, making continued personal-data processing potentially impossible. 09_exit.md section 2.2; 03_dpa.md section 8.2
The Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md section 5.3; 03_dpa.md

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months’ Fees and says that cap prevails notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, the SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000, and the DPA disapplies all limitations for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

The SOW excludes indirect and consequential loss, while the DPA indemnity for fines and unlimited liability for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches may override or conflict with that exclusion for data-related losses. 02_sow.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 11
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA uses England and Wales law, while the DPA says both that it follows the Agreement law and that the DPA and disputes under it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md section 15.1; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

The DPA is internally contradictory on governing law because clause 13.1 points to the Agreement’s law except as provided in 13.2, and clause 13.2 then applies Irish law to the entire DPA and any dispute arising out of it. 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Change approval conflicts with the MSA: the MSA requires any change to Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while the Change Control Procedure allows deemed approval by silence, unilateral Provider approval up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md sections 4.2-4.4 and 6.1

The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17 and contains no Change Control Board provision. 08_change_control.md section 4.1; 01_msa.md

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected Change Requests at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan contains no specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md

The rate for rejected-change impact assessments is ambiguous because the Exit Plan only states a transition-assistance rate of £1,250 per person per day, while the Pricing Schedule standard rate is £1,450 per person per day and role-specific rates also vary. 08_change_control.md section 7.2; 09_exit.md section 3.2; 10_pricing.md section 2; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 3

The Acceptable Use Policy permits Provider to amend the policy on 30 days’ notice with acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes to Services be agreed in writing by both parties and the Change Control Procedure for changes. 11_acceptable_use.md section 8; 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md

Provider’s right to disclose Customer content to law enforcement or regulators without notice conflicts with the MSA confidentiality obligation, which permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know and contains no law-enforcement exception. 11_acceptable_use.md section 6; 01_msa.md section 11.2

Provider’s right to disclose Customer content where it considers disclosure required by law may conflict with the DPA requirement to process Customer Personal Data only on Customer’s documented instructions, unless a legal compulsion exception is implied but not stated. 11_acceptable_use.md section 6.1; 03_dpa.md section 2.2

The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing personal data relating to persons under 16, while the DPA processing scope includes Customer retail customers without any age limitation; the permitted processing population is therefore inconsistent or incomplete. 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.1; 03_dpa.md sections 3.2 and Annex 1

Information Security Policy data-location rules conflict with DPA approved locations: the policy allows storage/processing in any Provider region determined by Provider’s CISO, while the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin. 06_infosec.md section 2.1; 03_dpa.md sections 4.1-4.3 and Annex 2

Information Security Policy notice of adding a new region within 30 days after it enters service conflicts with the DPA requirement for prior written authorisation before transfers outside approved territories. 06_infosec.md section 2.3; 03_dpa.md section 4.2

The definition of “Subprocessor” conflicts: the DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

The definition of “Security Incident” in the Glossary overrides other definitions if effective, but that would make SLA and DPA incident triggers much broader than their own text, creating uncertainty in incident obligations. 15_glossary.md section 2; 03_dpa.md section 1.6; 04_sla.md section 7.1

The BCDR Plan suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes related unavailability from availability calculations, potentially conflicting with the SLA’s monthly availability commitment and service credit regime, which do not contain that exclusion except for maintenance and specified exclusions. 07_bcdr.md sections 5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md sections 3-4 and 9

BCDR RTO of eight hours conflicts or is at least not aligned with the SLA Priority 1 Resolution target of four hours for complete platform unavailability. 07_bcdr.md section 2.1; 04_sla.md sections 1.3 and 5.1

The BCDR Plan excludes unavailability from Continuity Events and return to primary environment from availability calculations, while the SLA’s exclusions do not expressly include Continuity Events. 07_bcdr.md section 5.3; 04_sla.md section 9

The DPA processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the Exit Plan contemplates transition services and Customer-data retention after termination, creating uncertainty over the lawful basis and contractual terms for post-termination processing. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3

The Order Form purchase-order clause allows invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, potentially conflicting with the MSA/SOW obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the stated payment period. 05_order_form.md section 5.3; 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3

The MSA assigns IP in Deliverables only “on payment in full for them”, but the pricing structure is recurring monthly fees and does not allocate specific prices to individual Deliverables, making the trigger for IP assignment unclear. 01_msa.md section 7.2; 02_sow.md section 5; 10_pricing.md section 1

The Glossary says references to documents are to those documents as amended from time to time, while several documents require formal change approval or written agreement for changes, creating uncertainty over whether unilateral or informal amendments are incorporated. 15_glossary.md section 3.3; 01_msa.md section 2.4; 08_change_control.md

The Approved Subprocessor List is maintained and published on Provider’s trust portal, which may allow the operative subprocessor list to change outside the executed contract set and conflicts with the DPA’s specific prior-consent requirement. 12_subprocessors.md sections 1.2 and 3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

The Information Security Policy requires deletion of security logs after 18 months, but those logs may be needed for audits or investigations under the DPA and for records sufficient to demonstrate compliance under the MSA. 06_infosec.md section 5.2; 03_dpa.md section 9; 01_msa.md sections 10.1 and 12.4

The Pricing Schedule says service credits under any Schedule are deducted from the next recurring invoice, but the MSA/SOW invoicing in arrears and Pricing Schedule invoicing in advance conflict over what the “next” invoice is and when credits are applied. 10_pricing.md section 4.1; 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 10_pricing.md section 1.2

The SOW says Provider shall deliver a 36-month programme, but the Order Form initial term is only 12 months and the MSA initial term is 24 months; no provision reconciles what happens to unfinished phases if the shorter term ends or is not renewed. 02_sow.md sections 2.1 and 4; 05_order_form.md section 1.2; 01_msa.md section 3.1
unmatched: The document set is internally inconsistent about how many documents form the contract: the prompt refers to four documents, but fifteen documents are supplied and several later documents purport to be schedules/exhibits/addenda to the MSA. Overall contract set

The scope of reimbursable expenses conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and requires prior approval for expenses outside the Fee, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and only requires approval above £500 per month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2 and 5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1 and 3.2

Volume-based transaction charges conflict with the SOW statement that the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise; the SOW does not identify transaction overage charges. 02_sow.md section 5.2; 10_pricing.md sections 5.1-5.2

Confidentiality duration is unclear for personal data and broadly defined confidential information because the MSA confidentiality obligation lasts only three years after termination, while the DPA and Glossary broaden the information covered without stating the same duration or a different one. 01_msa.md section 11.3; 03_dpa.md section 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2

findings: The prompt says the contract set consists of four documents, but the supplied set contains fifteen documents numbered 01 through 15, creating uncertainty as to the intended contract set. Document set / headings

Circular and inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda, the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says the Order Form prevails over all other documents and ranks Addenda last, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over all other definitions despite being only a Schedule. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2; 05_order_form.md §2; 15_glossary.md §1.2
The MSA definition of Agreement does not include the Order Form or Exhibits, while the Glossary definition includes the Order Form, Schedules, Exhibits and Addenda. 01_msa.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

The MSA initial term is 24 months from 1 April 2027, the SOW programme is 36 months commencing 1 March 2027, and the Order Form initial term is 12 months from 1 April 2027. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §§1.2-1.3

The SOW commences on 1 March 2027, before the MSA Effective Date of 1 April 2027 and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §7.3

Termination/non-renewal notice periods conflict: the MSA requires 90 days' notice for convenience termination, the SOW requires 30 days' notice for convenience termination, and the Order Form requires only 30 days' notice of non-renewal. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3; 05_order_form.md §6.2

Monthly recurring charge conflicts: MSA states £12,400, SOW states £12,800, Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 implies £12,800/month, and Pricing Schedule states £13,100/month. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: MSA, SOW and Order Form say monthly in arrears, while Pricing Schedule says recurring charges are invoiced monthly in advance and invoices are issued on the first Business Day of each month. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.5; 10_pricing.md §§1.2, 6.1

Payment terms conflict: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW requires 45 days of receipt, and Order Form requires 60 days from date of invoice. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Fee increase provisions conflict: MSA permits annual CPI increases on 60 days' notice, while Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Expense provisions conflict: SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and requires prior approval for expenses outside the Fee, while Pricing Schedule generally permits travel and subsistence recovery at cost and requires prior approval only above £500/month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

The definition of Fee conflicts: MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under clause 4, while the Glossary expands Fee to all amounts payable under the Agreement, including recurring charges, T&M charges and expenses. 01_msa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2

Business Day is defined three incompatible ways: MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays; Glossary uses Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2
Acceptance criteria reference is broken: MSA requires assessment against Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Acceptance process conflicts: MSA requires express written acceptance, SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and requires a signed acceptance certificate after a 15 Business Day review. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§5.2-5.3

Deliverable source conflicts: SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2

Deliverable definition conflicts: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while Glossary defines Deliverables as any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md §1.3; 15_glossary.md §2
Deliverable warranty period conflicts: MSA warranty is 90 days after acceptance, while Exhibit A warranty is 180 days from acceptance. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Key personnel substitution provisions conflict: SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in certain cases. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1-2.4

Key personnel are said to be named in the programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set and the individuals are not otherwise named. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1

Team location conflicts: SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B locates the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London and only some key personnel in Bengaluru. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Data processing location obligations conflict with delivery location: DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and approved locations, while SOW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India, potentially requiring access to Customer Personal Data outside the permitted territories. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3; 02_sow.md §3.4

Data location provisions conflict: DPA permits processing only in the UK/EEA and approved locations, while the Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored and processed in any Provider region determined by Provider's CISO, with notice only after adding a region. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3; 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3
Approved processing locations conflict: DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin, while BCDR Plan uses Frankfurt, Germany as the secondary recovery environment. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md §3.1

Approved processing locations conflict with subprocessor list: DPA Annex 2 lists London and Dublin only, while the Subprocessor List includes Manchester and Singapore locations and says it is Annex 2 to the DPA. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md preamble and §2
The Subprocessor List incorrectly states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but DPA Annex 2 already exists and is titled Approved Processing Locations. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md preamble

Subprocessor consent provisions conflict: DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Subprocessor List allows Provider to add or replace Subprocessors on notice, to proceed despite unresolved objections, and to replace immediately with after-the-fact notice. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

Subcontracting consent provisions conflict: MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while DPA requires prior written consent for each Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

Audit rights conflict: MSA says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider's premises or systems beyond receiving SOC 2, while DPA gives annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

Records access is internally unclear: MSA requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit, inspection or attendance rights. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Record and data retention/deletion obligations conflict: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, while DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days, Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days, and Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2; 06_infosec.md §5.2
Exit Plan personal data reference is broken: it states personal data obligations are in DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md

Transition data retention is inconsistent with transition duration: Exit Plan says the transition period runs until six months after termination, but Customer data is retained for only 90 days following termination to support transition and data requests. 09_exit.md §§2.1, 2.3

Exit obligations conflict with DPA deletion: Exit Plan requires Provider to continue Services through a transition period ending six months after termination and to deliver Customer data by the end of that period, while DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days of expiry or termination. 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3, 4.1, 5.2

Liability caps conflict: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000; DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2; 03_dpa.md §11.1
Indirect/consequential loss exclusion in SOW conflicts with DPA clause saying no exclusion of liability applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 02_sow.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1
Insurance limits conflict: MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Governing law conflicts: MSA applies laws of England and Wales with exclusive English/Welsh courts, while DPA clause 13.2 applies Irish law to the DPA and disputes arising from it. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

Confidential Information definition conflicts: MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether marked or not, and Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or oral/written. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2

Confidentiality disclosure obligations conflict with Acceptable Use Policy: MSA permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, while AUP allows disclosure of Customer content to law enforcement or regulators without notice where Provider considers it required. 01_msa.md §11.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2

AUP lawful disclosure may conflict with DPA processing-on-instructions requirement where Customer content includes Customer Personal Data, because Provider may disclose without Customer instruction or notice. 03_dpa.md §2.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers confirmed unauthorised access resulting in loss or corruption; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation, and Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1
SLA references escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md

Availability service level conflicts: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability from Phase 3, while SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability and the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md §§7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1; 05_order_form.md §3.3

Support coverage conflicts: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and Business Day 08:00-18:00 support for Priority 2 and 3, while Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

Key personnel are said to be named in the programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set and the individuals are not otherwise named. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1
Indirect/consequential loss exclusion in SOW conflicts with DPA clause saying no exclusion of liability applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 02_sow.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1

AUP lawful disclosure may conflict with DPA processing-on-instructions requirement where Customer content includes Customer Personal Data, because Provider may disclose without Customer instruction or notice. 03_dpa.md §2.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2

SLA response-time measurement is internally defective: response and Resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response target run from the act that constitutes or follows the response itself. 04_sla.md §§5.1-5.4

Rejected-change assessment charge is unclear: Change Control says Provider may charge for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md

Subprocessor definition conflicts: DPA defines Subprocessor as a third party processing Customer Personal Data, while Glossary defines it as a third party processing Personal Data generally, which could include personal data outside Customer Personal Data. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

Order Form payment term from invoice date conflicts with MSA/SOW payment term from receipt, making due dates differ if invoice date and receipt date differ. 05_order_form.md §1.6; 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, while Exit Plan requires Services and data handling to continue during a transition period after termination, creating uncertainty whether post-termination transition processing is authorised. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

Subcontracting consent conflicts with data processing controls: the MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent for each Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md section 9.3; 03_dpa.md section 5.1

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audit rights including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md section 10.2; 03_dpa.md sections 9.1-9.2

The MSA records clause is internally inconsistent because Provider must make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no audit/inspection rights beyond receiving the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md sections 10.2 and 12.2

Record/data retention and deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination, the Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days after termination, the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months, and several schedules require records only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md section 12.4; 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md sections 2.3 and 5.2; 06_infosec.md section 5.2; 04_sla.md section 6.3; 08_change_control.md section 9.3
The Exit Plan refers to personal data obligations in DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md section 5.3; 03_dpa.md

The DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days of expiry or termination, while the Exit Plan requires Provider to continue Services through a transition period ending 6 months after termination and to retain Customer data for 90 days after termination. These obligations cannot all be satisfied for personal data. 03_dpa.md section 8.2; 09_exit.md sections 2.1-2.3 and 5.2

The Exit Plan says it applies on expiry as well as termination, but defines the transition period as beginning on the date notice of termination is given, leaving no clear transition-period start date for expiry without termination notice. 09_exit.md sections 1.2 and 2.1

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; the SOW caps liability at £250,000; and the DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md sections 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md section 9.2; 03_dpa.md section 11.1
Insurance requirements conflict: the MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md section 16.1; 02_sow.md section 9.4

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies the laws of England and Wales with exclusive England and Wales jurisdiction, while the DPA states that the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md sections 15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md sections 13.1-13.2

Availability service levels conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% availability from Phase 3, the SLA requires 99.9% monthly availability, and the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md sections 7.1-7.2; 04_sla.md section 3.1; 05_order_form.md section 3.3

Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps credits at 10% of the monthly Fee, and the Pricing Schedule caps all service credits at 5% of the recurring monthly charge. 02_sow.md section 7.4; 04_sla.md section 4.2; 10_pricing.md section 4.2

Service credit remedy language conflicts: the SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, while the DPA removes liability limitations/exclusions for DPA and Data Protection Law breaches, which could include availability/security failures involving personal data. 04_sla.md section 4.3; 03_dpa.md section 11.1

Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and Business Day support for Priority 2 and 3, while the Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md sections 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md section 3.1

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point at which Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because acknowledgement is itself the response trigger. 04_sla.md section 5.4

The BCDR Plan suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes related unavailability from availability calculations, while the SLA availability exclusions do not include Continuity Events or BCDR invocation. 04_sla.md sections 3.2-3.3 and 9; 07_bcdr.md section 5

The BCDR Plan sets an 8-hour RTO, while the SLA requires Priority 1 Resolution within 4 hours. A Continuity Event that is also a Priority 1 Incident is subject to incompatible restoration targets unless the BCDR suspension prevails. 04_sla.md section 5.1; 07_bcdr.md sections 2.1 and 5.1

Team location commitments conflict: the SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B lists the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect as based full-time in London. 02_sow.md section 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1

Key personnel substitution rights conflict: the SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md sections 2.1-2.4

The SOW refers to named key personnel, and Exhibit B says the individuals are named in the programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set. 02_sow.md section 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1.1

The MSA requires Customer to nominate a single point of contact, while the Order Form lists separate commercial and technical contacts and the SOW refers to Customer's nominated contact, creating uncertainty as to which contact controls notices/reviews/acceptance. 01_msa.md section 5.2; 02_sow.md section 6.2; 05_order_form.md sections 4.1-4.2

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement or regulators without notice, while the MSA confidentiality clause contains no corresponding exception permitting disclosure of Confidential Information to such bodies. 01_msa.md section 11.2; 11_acceptable_use.md section 6

The Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, while the Information Security Policy defines payment card data as Restricted Data and sets controls for it, creating ambiguity over whether payment card data is permitted if secured or prohibited entirely. 11_acceptable_use.md section 3.2; 06_infosec.md sections 1.2 and 3

The Glossary defines Subprocessor as a third party engaged to process Personal Data generally, while the DPA defines it as a third party engaged to process Customer Personal Data specifically. 03_dpa.md section 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2

The Glossary defines Personal Data by reference to the UK GDPR, while the DPA defines Data Protection Law as all law applicable in the territories in which Services are provided. This may conflict where processing occurs outside the UK or under non-UK data protection regimes. 03_dpa.md sections 1.2-1.3; 15_glossary.md section 2

The Pricing Schedule requires invoice queries within 10 Business Days of receipt, but other payment clauses require payment only of undisputed invoices within longer periods. The consequence of failing to query within 10 Business Days is not reconciled with the right to dispute invoices. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 02_sow.md section 5.3; 05_order_form.md section 1.6; 10_pricing.md section 6.3

The Order Form states invoices without a valid purchase order number may be returned unpaid, while the MSA requires payment of undisputed invoices within 30 days and does not make a purchase order number a condition of payment. 01_msa.md section 4.3; 05_order_form.md sections 5.2-5.3
unmatched: Expense recovery conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers all travel unless expressly stated otherwise and outside expenses require prior approval, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md sections 5.2 and 5.4; 10_pricing.md sections 3.1-3.2
