findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule/Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2

Precedence conflict: the Order Form ranks Addenda below Schedules and the MSA, while the DPA contains terms intended to override the Agreement, especially liability and governing law. 05_order_form.md §2.1; 03_dpa.md §§11.1, 13.2

Precedence conflict: the Glossary, although only Schedule 10 and ranked below the MSA by the Order Form/MSA, says its definitions prevail over every other document. 15_glossary.md §1.2; 05_order_form.md §2.1; 01_msa.md §14.2

The contract set is internally inconsistent about what documents form the Agreement: the MSA includes only the MSA, Schedules and Addenda; the Order Form treats itself as part of the agreement; the Glossary adds Exhibits. 01_msa.md §1.1; 05_order_form.md §2.1; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Agreement”
The same defined term “Business Day” is defined three different ways. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Business Day”

The same defined term “Confidential Information” is defined inconsistently: marked written information only, all Customer Personal Data whether marked or not, and all information whether oral or written. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Confidential Information”

The same defined term “Deliverable” is defined inconsistently: only items identified in a SOW, items in a delivery-lead phase plan, listed Exhibit A deliverables, and any output of the Services. 01_msa.md §1.3; 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Deliverable”

The same defined term “Fee” is defined inconsistently: amounts payable under MSA clause 4 only versus all amounts payable under the Agreement including expenses and time-and-materials charges. 01_msa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Fee”

The same defined term “Services” is defined inconsistently: services described in a SOW only versus SOW services plus support services in the SLA schedule. 01_msa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Services”
The same defined term “Security Incident” is defined inconsistently across the DPA, SLA and Glossary. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Security Incident”

The same defined term “Subprocessor” is defined inconsistently: a third party processing Customer Personal Data versus a third party processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Subprocessor”
The MSA initial term is 24 months, the Order Form initial term is 12 months, and SOW 1 describes a 36-month programme. 01_msa.md §3.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2; 02_sow.md §2.1
SOW 1 commences before both the MSA Effective Date and the Order Form Service Commencement Date/signature date. 02_sow.md §2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md §§1.3, 7.3

Convenience termination periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days’ notice to terminate the Agreement, SOW 1 allows termination of the SOW on 30 days’ notice, and the Order Form allows non-renewal on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3; 05_order_form.md §6.2

Monthly recurring charges conflict: £12,400 in the MSA, £12,800 in SOW 1/Order Form annual value, and £13,100 in the Pricing Schedule. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: monthly in arrears in the MSA, SOW and Order Form, but monthly in advance in the Pricing Schedule. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.5; 10_pricing.md §1.2
Payment periods conflict: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Fee increase/indexation terms conflict: the MSA permits annual CPI increases on notice, while the Pricing Schedule fixes the recurring charge during the initial term with no indexation or increase. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Expenses terms conflict: SOW 1 says the Fee covers travel unless expressly stated otherwise and all outside-Fee expenses need prior written approval; the Pricing Schedule makes travel/subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Service credit caps conflict: SOW 1 allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps them at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps aggregate credits at 5%. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2; 10_pricing.md §4.2
Availability service levels conflict: SOW 1 requires 99.5% availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md §7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Service level start dates conflict: SOW 1 applies platform service levels from Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md §7.1; 05_order_form.md §3.3
Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1, while the Order Form says 24x7 support applies to all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

Acceptance provisions conflict: the MSA and Exhibit A require express/signed written acceptance and say silence is not acceptance, while SOW 1 provides deemed acceptance after five Business Days of silence. 01_msa.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.3; 02_sow.md §6.3

Acceptance review periods conflict: SOW 1 allows five Business Days before deemed acceptance, while Exhibit A gives Customer fifteen Business Days to assess a Deliverable. 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.2
The MSA points to acceptance criteria in “Schedule 1, Section 12,” but SOW 1/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables source conflicts: SOW 1 says deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2
Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA gives a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives 180 days. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Key-personnel substitution terms conflict: SOW 1 requires Customer’s prior written agreement for substitutions, while Exhibit B permits substitution on notice and in some cases immediately. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1, 2.4

Personnel location commitments conflict: SOW 1 says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, but Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Data processing locations conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and approved locations London/Dublin, while SOW 1 places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India. 03_dpa.md §§4.1, Annex 2; 02_sow.md §3.4

Data processing location terms conflict: the Information Security Policy allows Customer data to be stored/processed in any Provider region chosen by Provider’s CISO, while the DPA restricts Customer Personal Data to the UK/EEA and listed approved locations. 06_infosec.md §2.1; 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3, Annex 2
The BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt is not listed as an approved processing location in the DPA Annex 2, which lists only London and Dublin. 07_bcdr.md §3.1; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

The Approved Subprocessor List includes a Singapore subprocessor, conflicting with the DPA’s UK/EEA-only processing and approved-location restrictions unless separately authorised. 12_subprocessors.md §2; 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3, Annex 2

Subprocessor approval processes conflict: the DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Approved Subprocessor List permits additions/replacements on notice with an objection right and even immediate replacement in some cases. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

Subcontracting terms conflict: the MSA permits subcontracting without prior consent, while the DPA requires prior written consent for Subprocessors processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1
The Approved Subprocessor List says it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA’s Annex 2 is already “Approved Processing Locations,” not subprocessors. 12_subprocessors.md preamble; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection rights beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA grants annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

Records access is internally inconsistent: the MSA requires records to be made available on reasonable request “in accordance with clause 10.2,” but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further audit, inspection or attendance rights. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Retention/deletion obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for seven years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days and the Exit Plan requires deletion after a 90-day retention period and handover. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2

Security-log retention conflicts with the MSA’s seven-year retention requirement: the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. 06_infosec.md §5.2; 01_msa.md §12.4

Service-report retention conflicts with the MSA’s seven-year retention requirement: the SLA requires service reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement. 04_sla.md §6.3; 01_msa.md §12.4

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: 24 hours from awareness under the DPA, 72 hours from confirmation under the SLA, and 48 hours from confirmation under the Information Security Policy. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA contains no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies England and Wales law and exclusive courts, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §13.2

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps liability by reference to 12 months’ Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, SOW 1 sets a £250,000 cap, and the DPA disapplies all limitations/exclusions for DPA or data-protection breaches. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2; 03_dpa.md §11.1

Exclusion/indemnity conflict: SOW 1 excludes indirect or consequential loss, while the DPA says no exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches and includes an indemnity for fines. 02_sow.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §§11.1-11.2
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW 1 requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Change approval terms conflict: the MSA requires any Service change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while the Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval by silence, unilateral Provider approval up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §§4.2-4.4, 6.1
The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md §4.1; 01_msa.md

The Change Control Procedure allows Provider’s Delivery Lead to approve changes without Customer approval up to £35,000, conflicting with Customer-payment/approval controls and the MSA’s bilateral change requirement. 08_change_control.md §4.3; 01_msa.md §2.4

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected changes at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a rate for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md

Transition assistance rate conflicts with the Pricing Schedule rate card: the Exit Plan sets £1,250 per person per day, while the Pricing Schedule standard rate is £1,450 per person per day unless Exhibit B role-specific rates apply. 09_exit.md §3.2; 10_pricing.md §2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3
The Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal-data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md

Exit transition obligations conflict with termination mechanics: the Exit Plan requires Services to continue from notice through six months after the effective termination date, including after termination for breach, while the MSA allows immediate termination for uncured material breach. 09_exit.md §§1.2, 2.1-2.2; 01_msa.md §3.4

Exit data retention conflicts with DPA deletion: the Exit Plan requires Customer data retention for 90 days following termination to support transition, while the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days of expiry/termination. 09_exit.md §2.3; 03_dpa.md §8.2

Service credit remedy provisions conflict: the SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failure, while the MSA/DPA liability provisions and SOW commercial protections do not preserve that sole-remedy limitation and contain inconsistent liability regimes. 04_sla.md §4.3; 01_msa.md §13; 02_sow.md §9; 03_dpa.md §11

The BCDR Plan excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations and suspends SLA obligations, which conflicts with the SLA’s general availability commitment unless read as an additional unranked exclusion. 07_bcdr.md §§5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md §§3.1-3.3, 9

The BCDR Plan allows up to 12 hours of planned unavailability for return to the primary environment, but the SLA requires at least five Business Days’ notice of a maintenance window; the return window may be impossible to notice in advance after a disaster. 07_bcdr.md §5.2; 04_sla.md §3.4

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the policy on 30 days’ notice with acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA and Change Control Procedure requirement for agreed change control. 11_acceptable_use.md §8; 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md

The Acceptable Use Policy permits Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without notice, conflicting with the MSA confidentiality restriction on third-party disclosure except to personnel who need to know. 11_acceptable_use.md §6; 01_msa.md §11.2

The Acceptable Use Policy allows immediate suspension for suspected policy breach with charges continuing, but the SLA contains no corresponding exclusion from availability/service credits for such suspension. 11_acceptable_use.md §§5.1-5.4; 04_sla.md §§3, 4, 9

The MSA requires Provider to comply with Customer’s reasonable instructions as to manner of performance, while several later documents allow Provider unilateral control inconsistent with that requirement, including data regions, subprocessor changes, AUP changes and low-value change approvals. 01_msa.md §2.3; 06_infosec.md §2.1; 12_subprocessors.md §3; 11_acceptable_use.md §8; 08_change_control.md §4.3

The DPA says Provider shall process Customer Personal Data only on Customer’s documented instructions, but the Information Security Policy permits Provider to choose processing regions and the Approved Subprocessor List permits certain subprocessor changes without prior written authorisation. 03_dpa.md §2.2; 06_infosec.md §2.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

The SOW says the delivery lead must be available during Customer’s working hours, but the delivery team is stated to operate from Bengaluru and the SLA/Order Form require support coverage extending beyond ordinary Customer working hours; responsibilities and coverage are inconsistent. 02_sow.md §§3.3-3.4; 04_sla.md §2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

Exhibit B says Key Personnel are named in the programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set, leaving named Key Personnel unidentified. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1
Exhibit A acceptance criteria depend on external documents not included in the contract set, including the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3
SOW 1 acceptance depends on a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, but that phase plan is not included and appears capable of unilateral maintenance by Provider. 02_sow.md §6.1

The Glossary definition of “Business Day” includes public holidays, which conflicts with support and notice provisions elsewhere that plainly intend public holidays to be excluded. 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Business Day”; 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1

The Glossary’s broad definition of “Security Incident” expands SLA and DPA incident obligations beyond their narrower definitions, creating uncertainty over which notification trigger and deadline applies. 15_glossary.md §2 definition of “Security Incident”; 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1

The Pricing Schedule says service credits under any Schedule are deducted from the next recurring invoice, but the MSA/SOW invoices are monthly in arrears and the Pricing Schedule invoices monthly in advance, making the “next recurring invoice” timing uncertain. 10_pricing.md §§1.2, 4.1; 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3

The Order Form requires invoices to include a purchase order and allows return unpaid if missing, which qualifies or conflicts with the MSA’s obligation to pay undisputed invoices within 30 days of receipt. 05_order_form.md §§5.2-5.3; 01_msa.md §4.3

The MSA prohibits set-off/deduction except by law or Provider agreement, while service-credit provisions require credits/deductions from invoices automatically or as entitlement. 01_msa.md §4.5; 04_sla.md §4.1; 10_pricing.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §7.4

The Approved Subprocessor List includes Ashcombe Payments for payment tokenisation, while the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits Customer storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform, making the payment-tokenisation processing scope unclear. 12_subprocessors.md §2; 11_acceptable_use.md §3.2

Information Security Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data, while the Acceptable Use Policy forbids storage of payment card primary account numbers; the documents do not reconcile whether any payment card data may be processed and under what conditions. 06_infosec.md §1.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §3.2

The DPA Annex 1 processing duration is the term of the Agreement, while the Exit Plan requires post-termination transition services and data retention; the lawful processing basis during the post-termination transition period is unclear. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected changes at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a rate for impact assessments. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md

Exit transition obligations conflict with termination mechanics: the Exit Plan requires Services to continue from notice through six months after the effective termination date, including after termination for breach, while the MSA allows immediate termination for uncured material breach. 09_exit.md §§1.2, 2.1-2.2; 01_msa.md §3.4

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while SOW 1 says the SOW prevails over the MSA. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md clause 1.2

Inconsistent precedence: the Order Form says it prevails over every other document and ranks Addenda below Schedules, conflicting with the MSA's MSA-over-Schedule/Addendum rule and the DPA's role as an Addendum. 05_order_form.md clauses 2.1-2.2; 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 03_dpa.md clause 12.1

Inconsistent precedence for definitions: the Glossary says its definitions prevail over any other document, conflicting with the MSA and Order Form precedence clauses. 15_glossary.md clause 1.2; 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 05_order_form.md clause 2.2
The MSA definition of Agreement omits the Order Form and Exhibits, while the Glossary includes the Order Form and all Exhibits/Addenda. 01_msa.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md definition of "Agreement"
The initial term is inconsistent: the MSA has a 24-month initial term, while the Order Form has a 12-month initial term. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 05_order_form.md clause 1.2

The SOW requires a 36-month programme, which is longer than both the MSA's 24-month initial term and the Order Form's 12-month initial term. 02_sow.md clause 2.1; 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 05_order_form.md clause 1.2
The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date. 02_sow.md clause 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md clause 7.3

Exit obligations conflict with DPA deletion: Provider must continue Services throughout the post-termination transition period and deliver Customer data by the end of that period, but DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after termination. 09_exit.md clauses 2.1-2.2 and 4.1; 03_dpa.md clause 8.2
Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md clause 5.3; 03_dpa.md

Liability caps conflict: MSA caps liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies despite any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps liability at £250,000; DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA or Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md clause 9.2; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1

The SOW's exclusion of indirect/consequential loss may conflict with the DPA indemnity for fines resulting from data-protection breaches if such fines are argued to be excluded or limited elsewhere. 02_sow.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 11.2
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md clause 9.4
Governing law conflicts: MSA applies England and Wales law and exclusive jurisdiction; DPA says it is governed by Republic of Ireland law. 01_msa.md clauses 15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1-13.2

DPA governing-law clause is internally defective: clause 13.1 says the DPA follows the Agreement's law except as clause 13.2 provides, while clause 13.2 states the whole DPA and any dispute are governed by Irish law, effectively overriding clause 13.1. 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1-13.2
Availability level conflicts: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability; SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md clause 7.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.1

Service level start date conflicts: SOW applies service levels only from Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md clause 7.1; 05_order_form.md clause 3.3

Support coverage conflicts: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1, with limited Business Day hours for Priority 2 and 3; Order Form says support is 24x7 for all priority levels. 04_sla.md clauses 2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md clause 3.1

Service credit caps conflict: SOW allows credits up to 25% of monthly Fee, SLA caps them at 10%, and Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly credits at 5%. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clause 4.2; 10_pricing.md clause 4.2

Service credit remedy language conflicts: SLA says service credits are Customer's sole financial remedy for availability failures, but DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches and MSA has a different liability regime. 04_sla.md clause 4.3; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1; 01_msa.md clause 13

Service credit application conflicts: SLA requires automatic application to the next invoice, while SOW merely says Customer is entitled to credits of up to 25% and Pricing Schedule applies a different aggregate cap. 04_sla.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 10_pricing.md clause 4.2

SLA response/resolution measurement is internally defective because times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement, so Provider can delay acknowledgement and the response target is measured from the response/acknowledgement itself. 04_sla.md clause 5.4

Security Incident notification timing conflicts: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness; Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation; SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 06_infosec.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3
SLA Security Incident escalation contact reference is defective: it refers to Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md clause 7.4; 03_dpa.md

SLA Security Incident definition is narrower than the DPA and Glossary definitions, so the same event may trigger different obligations depending on document. 04_sla.md clause 7.1; 03_dpa.md clause 1.6; 15_glossary.md definition of "Security Incident"

BCDR availability exclusions conflict with SLA availability calculation: BCDR excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability, while SLA excludes only agreed maintenance windows and specified exclusions. 07_bcdr.md clauses 5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md clauses 3.2-3.3 and 9

BCDR allows up to 12 hours of planned unavailability to return to the primary environment, but SLA requires at least 5 Business Days' notice of a maintenance window and does not expressly treat BCDR return activity as agreed maintenance. 07_bcdr.md clause 5.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.4

BCDR RTO of 8 hours conflicts with SLA Priority 1 Resolution target of 4 hours for outages, unless Provider invokes BCDR and suspends SLA obligations. 07_bcdr.md clauses 2.1 and 5.1; 04_sla.md clause 5.1
BCDR refers to reviewing a dependency list at each annual test, but no dependency list is included in the Plan. 07_bcdr.md clause 8.3

Confidentiality disclosure provisions conflict: MSA permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, while DPA/Subprocessor documents require disclosure to subprocessors, and the Acceptable Use Policy permits disclosure to law enforcement/regulators without notice. 01_msa.md clause 11.2; 03_dpa.md clause 5; 12_subprocessors.md; 11_acceptable_use.md clause 6

AUP lawful disclosure conflicts with DPA processing-on-instructions obligation because Provider may disclose Customer content where it considers disclosure required, without Customer instruction or notice. 11_acceptable_use.md clauses 6.1-6.2; 03_dpa.md clause 2.2

Provider's no-monitoring obligation conflicts with security classification duties: AUP says Provider does not monitor Customer content, while Information Security Policy requires Provider to classify all Customer data on receipt as Restricted or Internal. 11_acceptable_use.md clause 4.1; 06_infosec.md clause 1.4

Restricted/payment-card data provisions are inconsistent: Information Security Policy treats payment card data as Restricted Data to be protected, while AUP prohibits Customer from storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform. 06_infosec.md clause 1.2; 11_acceptable_use.md clause 3.2

Pricing Schedule role-rate hierarchy conflicts with Exit Plan transition rate: Pricing/Exhibit B set standard and role-specific day rates, while Exit Plan sets a different £1,250 per person per day transition assistance rate. 10_pricing.md clauses 2.1-2.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 3; 09_exit.md clause 3.2

The Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 matches the SOW monthly Fee of £12,800 but conflicts with the Pricing Schedule's £13,100 monthly recurring charge, which would total £157,200 annually before any usage charges. 05_order_form.md clause 1.4; 02_sow.md clause 5.1; 10_pricing.md clause 1.1
Service Commencement Date conflicts with SOW programme start: Order Form starts services on 1 April 2027, but SOW programme starts on 1 March 2027. 05_order_form.md clause 1.3; 02_sow.md clause 2.2

The Glossary definition of Business Day includes public holidays, which makes deadlines in documents that expressly exclude public holidays inconsistent or uncertain. 15_glossary.md definition of "Business Day"; 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1

The Glossary definition of Confidential Information makes unmarked and oral information confidential, conflicting with the MSA's marking-in-writing requirement and altering the confidentiality survival scope. 15_glossary.md definition of "Confidential Information"; 01_msa.md clauses 11.1-11.3

The Glossary definition of Deliverable expands Deliverables to any output, conflicting with the acceptance and IP provisions that depend on identified Deliverables. 15_glossary.md definition of "Deliverable"; 01_msa.md clauses 1.3, 6 and 7.2

The Subprocessor List permits Provider to maintain and publish the current list on its trust portal, but DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor rather than unilateral portal maintenance. 12_subprocessors.md clauses 1.2 and 3.1; 03_dpa.md clause 5.1

The AUP suspension right allows immediate suspension without prior notice and charges continue, which conflicts with service-level availability/support commitments that do not expressly exclude AUP suspensions from downtime. 11_acceptable_use.md clauses 5.1-5.4; 04_sla.md clauses 3 and 9

The AUP prohibition on storing personal data relating to persons under 16 may be incompatible with the DPA's processing description for Customer retail customers, which contains no age limitation. 11_acceptable_use.md clause 3.1; 03_dpa.md clauses 3.2-3.3 and Annex 1
unmatched: The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date. 02_sow.md clause 2.2; 01_msa.md Effective Date; 05_order_form.md clause 7.3

Expense recovery conflicts: SOW says the Fee covers travel unless expressly stated otherwise and any outside expenses require prior written approval; Pricing Schedule allows travel/subsistence at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md clauses 5.2-5.4; 10_pricing.md clauses 3.1-3.2
The MSA requires changes to be agreed before implementation, but the Change Control Procedure allows emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md clause 2.4; 08_change_control.md clause 6.1

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for rejected change impact assessments at the rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan contains no rate for rejected change impact assessments. 08_change_control.md clause 7.2; 09_exit.md
Definition of Business Day conflicts across documents. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md definition of "Business Day"

Definition of Subprocessor conflicts: DPA covers third parties processing Customer Personal Data; Glossary covers third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md clause 1.5; 15_glossary.md definition of "Subprocessor"

Resubmission timing conflicts: SOW requires Provider to address comments and resubmit within 10 Business Days; Exhibit A gives a fresh 15 Business Day assessment period after remedy/resubmission but does not align with the 10-day remedy period. 02_sow.md clause 6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clause 5.4

Key personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says the individuals are named in a programme initiation document, but that document is not included. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md clause 1.1; 02_sow.md clause 3.5

Service report/change log retention conflicts with MSA retention: SLA and Change Control Procedure retain reports/logs only for the duration of the Agreement, while MSA requires 7-year post-termination retention. 04_sla.md clause 6.3; 08_change_control.md clause 9.3; 01_msa.md clause 12.4

DPA governing-law clause is internally defective: clause 13.1 says the DPA follows the Agreement's law except as clause 13.2 provides, while clause 13.2 states the whole DPA and any dispute are governed by Irish law, effectively overriding clause 13.1. 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1-13.2

SLA response/resolution measurement is internally defective because times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement, so Provider can delay acknowledgement and the response target is measured from the response/acknowledgement itself. 04_sla.md clause 5.4
BCDR refers to reviewing a dependency list at each annual test, but no dependency list is included in the Plan. 07_bcdr.md clause 8.3

AUP lawful disclosure conflicts with DPA processing-on-instructions obligation because Provider may disclose Customer content where it considers disclosure required, without Customer instruction or notice. 11_acceptable_use.md clauses 6.1-6.2; 03_dpa.md clause 2.2

The Glossary definition of Business Day includes public holidays, which makes deadlines in documents that expressly exclude public holidays inconsistent or uncertain. 15_glossary.md definition of "Business Day"; 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1

The Glossary definition of Deliverable expands Deliverables to any output, conflicting with the acceptance and IP provisions that depend on identified Deliverables. 15_glossary.md definition of "Deliverable"; 01_msa.md clauses 1.3, 6 and 7.2

findings: Inconsistent order of precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda, the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form creates a different ranking, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over all other documents despite being only a Schedule. 01_msa.md §14.2; 02_sow.md §1.2; 05_order_form.md §2; 15_glossary.md §1.2

"Agreement" is defined inconsistently: the MSA definition excludes the Order Form and Exhibits, while the Glossary includes the Order Form, every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum. 01_msa.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

"Business Day" is defined three incompatible ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays, and Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

"Confidential Information" is defined inconsistently: the MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing, the DPA treats all Customer Personal Data as confidential whether marked or not, and the Glossary covers all information whether marked or oral/written. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2

"Deliverable" is defined inconsistently: the MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in an SOW, while the Glossary includes any output of the Services whether or not identified in an SOW. 01_msa.md §1.3; 15_glossary.md §2

"Fee" is defined inconsistently: the MSA ties it to amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while the Glossary includes all amounts payable under the Agreement, including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2
"Services" is defined inconsistently: the MSA limits Services to those described in an SOW, while the Glossary also includes support services under the SLA Schedule. 01_msa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

"Security Incident" is defined inconsistently: the DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; the SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access causing loss or corruption of Customer data; the Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 15_glossary.md §2

"Subprocessor" is defined inconsistently: the DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2
The initial term is inconsistent: the MSA has a 24-month initial term, while the Order Form states a 12-month Initial Term. 01_msa.md §3.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2
The SOW programme duration is 36 months, which is longer than both the MSA's 24-month initial term and the Order Form's 12-month Initial Term. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2

The SOW programme commences before the MSA Effective Date, before the Order Form signature date, and before the Order Form Service Commencement Date. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §§1.3, 7.3

Convenience termination/non-renewal periods conflict: the MSA requires 90 days' notice, the SOW can be terminated on 30 days' notice, and the Order Form permits non-renewal on 30 days' notice despite the MSA renewal clause requiring termination under the MSA. 01_msa.md §§3.2-3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3; 05_order_form.md §6
Monthly charges conflict: the MSA says £12,400, the SOW says £12,800, and the Pricing Schedule says £13,100. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 10_pricing.md §1.1

The Order Form Annual Contract Value of £153,600 equals £12,800 per month and therefore conflicts with the MSA monthly Fee of £12,400 and the Pricing Schedule monthly charge of £13,100. 01_msa.md §4.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Billing timing conflicts: the MSA, SOW and Order Form require monthly billing in arrears, while the Pricing Schedule requires monthly billing in advance. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.5; 10_pricing.md §1.2

Payment terms conflict: the MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, the SOW within 45 days of receipt, and the Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Fee increase provisions conflict: the MSA allows annual CPI increases on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Expenses provisions conflict: the SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and expenses outside the Fee require prior approval; the Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Service level start dates conflict: the SOW applies platform service levels only from the start of Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md §7.1; 05_order_form.md §3.3
Availability targets conflict: the SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md §7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps monthly credits at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly credits at 5%. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2; 10_pricing.md §4.2

Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1, with Priority 2 and 3 support limited to support hours on Business Days, while the Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

Priority 1/continuity recovery obligations conflict: the SLA requires Priority 1 Resolution within 4 hours, while the BCDR Plan allows an 8-hour RTO and suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event. 04_sla.md §5.1; 07_bcdr.md §§2.1, 5.1

The BCDR Plan excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations, adding exclusions not stated in the SOW/SLA availability regimes and potentially eliminating service credits for outages that would otherwise count. 02_sow.md §§7.3-7.4; 04_sla.md §§3.2-3.3, 4; 07_bcdr.md §5.3

The BCDR Plan permits up to 12 hours of planned unavailability for return to the primary environment without aligning with the SLA requirement for at least 5 Business Days' notice of maintenance windows. 04_sla.md §3.4; 07_bcdr.md §5.2
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Deliverables source conflicts: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2

Acceptance process conflicts: the MSA requires express written acceptance, the SOW provides deemed acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days and states silence does not constitute acceptance. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§5.2-5.3

Acceptance cure/resubmission timing conflicts: the SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments, while Exhibit A applies a new 15-Business-Day assessment period after remedy and resubmission without the same 10-day remedy obligation. 02_sow.md §6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.4

Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA provides a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A provides a 180-day warranty for accepted Deliverables. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Key personnel substitution provisions conflict: the SOW requires Customer's prior written agreement before substituting named key personnel, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in certain cases. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1-2.4

Delivery location conflicts: the SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B locates the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Named key personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says the individuals are named in the programme initiation document, which is not included, while the SOW imposes obligations on named key personnel. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4
Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps each party's aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees, while the SOW caps Provider liability under the SOW at £250,000. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2

The DPA excludes all Agreement liability limitations for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches, directly conflicting with the MSA clause stating the MSA liability cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 01_msa.md §13.3; 03_dpa.md §11.1

Governing law conflicts: the MSA provides for England and Wales law and exclusive courts, while the DPA states that the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §13.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA limits Customer to receiving Provider's SOC 2 Type II report and gives no further audit/inspection rights, while the DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

Assurance obligations conflict with the MSA's no-further-audit position: the Information Security Policy requires sharing penetration test reports and remediation plans, giving Customer additional assurance rights beyond the SOC 2-only regime. 01_msa.md §10.2; 06_infosec.md §§7.1-7.2

Record retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the SLA and Change Control Procedure retain service reports/change logs only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md §12.4; 04_sla.md §6.3; 08_change_control.md §9.3

Customer Personal Data deletion conflicts with other retention obligations: the DPA requires deletion within 30 days of expiry/termination, the Exit Plan requires retention for 90 days following termination, and the MSA requires retention of all records, data and materials for 7 years. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2

Security log retention conflicts with the MSA retention period: the Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months, while the MSA requires records/data/materials relating to the Agreement to be retained for 7 years after expiry/termination. 01_msa.md §12.4; 06_infosec.md §5.2

Processing location obligations conflict: the DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London/Dublin as approved locations, while the SOW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India. 02_sow.md §3.4; 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2
Disaster recovery location conflicts: the DPA's approved processing locations are London and Dublin, while the BCDR Plan uses a recovery environment in Frankfurt. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md §3.1

Data location provisions conflict: the DPA restricts processing to the UK/EEA and approved locations, while the Information Security Policy permits storage and processing in any Provider region selected by Provider's CISO, with notice only after a new region enters service. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3; 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3

The approved Subprocessor list includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, conflicting with the DPA's UK/EEA-only processing restriction and approved locations of London/Dublin. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md §2

Subcontracting/subprocessor consent provisions conflict: the MSA allows subcontracting without Customer consent, the DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, and the Subprocessor Schedule allows additions/replacements on notice with only an objection right and even allows Provider to proceed after unresolved objection. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

The Approved Subprocessor List states it is Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already has an Annex 2 titled Approved Processing Locations, creating duplicate and inconsistent Annex 2s. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md heading and introductory text

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: the DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, the SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming a Security Incident, and the Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1
The SLA refers to Security Incident escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md
The Exit Plan refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md

The Change Control Procedure refers to the Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17 and contains no Change Control Board provision. 08_change_control.md §4.1; 01_msa.md

Change approval provisions conflict with the MSA: the MSA requires both parties' written agreement before any change is implemented, while the Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead for changes up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §§4.2-4.4, 6.1

The Change Control Procedure permits Provider's Delivery Lead to approve changes with a cost impact up to £35,000 without Customer approval, conflicting with Customer payment/control protections and the MSA requirement for agreed written changes. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §4.3

The Change Control Procedure allows Provider to charge for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend that Policy on 30 days' notice with deemed acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation. 01_msa.md §2.4; 11_acceptable_use.md §§8.1-8.2

Information Security Policy and BCDR Plan change provisions permit material changes by notice only, conflicting with the MSA/change-control requirement for agreed written changes where the change affects Services or obligations. 01_msa.md §2.4; 06_infosec.md §10.2; 07_bcdr.md §9.3; 08_change_control.md §1.1

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because the response period starts only after acknowledgment. 04_sla.md §5.4

Customer contact provisions are incomplete/inconsistent: the MSA requires a single nominated point of contact, the Order Form lists multiple Customer contacts, and the SLA requires a nominated security contact but none is listed. 01_msa.md §5.2; 04_sla.md §7.3; 05_order_form.md §4

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without notifying Customer, conflicting with the MSA confidentiality restriction permitting disclosure only to personnel who need to know and with the DPA's documented-instructions processing model for Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §11.2; 03_dpa.md §2.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §6

The Exit Plan's 90-day post-termination data retention period is shorter than the transition period, which ends six months after the effective termination date, potentially requiring data deletion before transition assistance and exit milestones are complete. 09_exit.md §§2.1, 2.3, 5.2 and Annex 1

Exit data return format conflicts with DPA return rights: the Exit Plan requires Customer data in the format used by Provider's systems, while the DPA requires Customer Personal Data in a structured, commonly used format on request. 03_dpa.md §8.1; 09_exit.md §4.1(a)

Transition assistance rates conflict with the general rate card: the Exit Plan sets £1,250 per person per day, while the Pricing Schedule says time-and-materials work outside the recurring charge is billed at £1,450 per person per day unless Exhibit B sets a role-specific rate. 09_exit.md §3.2; 10_pricing.md §§2.1, 2.4

The BCDR Plan assumes continued availability of Provider's third-party infrastructure supplier, yet the Plan is supposed to restore Services after a disruptive event and the SLA/BCDR framework otherwise addresses platform unavailability; this assumption may exclude a core disaster scenario from the recovery commitment. 07_bcdr.md §§1.1, 8.1

The DPA Annex 1 processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the Agreement term is itself inconsistent across the MSA, Order Form and SOW, making the processing duration uncertain. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2
unmatched: "Subprocessor" is defined inconsistently: the DPA limits it to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

The SOW programme commences before the MSA Effective Date, before the Order Form signature date, and before the Order Form Service Commencement Date. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §§1.3, 7.3

Expenses provisions conflict: the SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and expenses outside the Fee require prior approval; the Pricing Schedule makes travel and subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Acceptance cure/resubmission timing conflicts: the SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments, while Exhibit A applies a new 15-Business-Day assessment period after remedy and resubmission without the same 10-day remedy obligation. 02_sow.md §6.4; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §5.4

The Change Control Procedure allows Provider to charge for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

Information Security Policy and BCDR Plan change provisions permit material changes by notice only, conflicting with the MSA/change-control requirement for agreed written changes where the change affects Services or obligations. 01_msa.md §2.4; 06_infosec.md §10.2; 07_bcdr.md §9.3; 08_change_control.md §1.1

The SLA measures response and resolution times from the point Provider acknowledges the Incident, making the response-time target circular or ineffective because the response period starts only after acknowledgment. 04_sla.md §5.4

Customer contact provisions are incomplete/inconsistent: the MSA requires a single nominated point of contact, the Order Form lists multiple Customer contacts, and the SLA requires a nominated security contact but none is listed. 01_msa.md §5.2; 04_sla.md §7.3; 05_order_form.md §4

The BCDR Plan assumes continued availability of Provider's third-party infrastructure supplier, yet the Plan is supposed to restore Services after a disruptive event and the SLA/BCDR framework otherwise addresses platform unavailability; this assumption may exclude a core disaster scenario from the recovery commitment. 07_bcdr.md §§1.1, 8.1

The DPA Annex 1 processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but the Agreement term is itself inconsistent across the MSA, Order Form and SOW, making the processing duration uncertain. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the Master Services Agreement says it prevails over any Schedule or Addendum, while Statement of Work 1 says it prevails over the Master Services Agreement. 01_msa.md clause 14.2; 02_sow.md clause 1.2

Order of precedence conflicts with the Glossary: the Order Form ranks Schedules below the MSA, but the Glossary, itself Schedule 10, says its definitions prevail over any other document. 05_order_form.md clause 2.1; 15_glossary.md clause 1.2
Order of precedence conflicts with the Statement of Work: the Order Form ranks the MSA above Schedules, while the SOW says it prevails over the MSA. 05_order_form.md clause 2.1; 02_sow.md clause 1.2

The Order Form is not clearly incorporated into the Agreement as defined in the MSA, because the MSA definition includes only the MSA, Schedules and Addenda, not order forms. 01_msa.md clause 1.1; 05_order_form.md generally; 15_glossary.md definition of Agreement

The definition of Agreement is inconsistent across documents: the MSA excludes the Order Form, while the Glossary includes the Order Form and every Schedule, Exhibit and Addendum. 01_msa.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Agreement

Initial term is inconsistent: MSA has a 24-month initial term, the Order Form has a 12-month initial term, and the SOW programme lasts 36 months. 01_msa.md clause 3.1; 05_order_form.md clause 1.2; 02_sow.md clause 2.1

Commencement dates conflict: the MSA and Order Form use 1 April 2027, while the SOW programme commences on 1 March 2027, before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md clause 2.2; 05_order_form.md clauses 1.3 and 7.3

Termination/non-renewal notice periods conflict: MSA convenience termination requires 90 days, SOW convenience termination requires 30 days, and Order Form non-renewal requires 30 days. 01_msa.md clause 3.3; 02_sow.md clause 2.3; 05_order_form.md clause 6.2

Monthly recurring charge is stated three different ways: £12,400 in the MSA, £12,800 in the SOW and implied by the Order Form annual contract value, and £13,100 in the Pricing and Rate Card. 01_msa.md clause 4.1; 02_sow.md clause 5.1; 05_order_form.md clause 1.4; 10_pricing.md clause 1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: MSA, SOW and Order Form say monthly in arrears, while the Pricing and Rate Card says monthly in advance on the first Business Day of each month. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3; 05_order_form.md clause 1.5; 10_pricing.md clauses 1.2 and 6.1

Payment terms conflict: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW within 45 days of receipt, and Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md clause 4.3; 02_sow.md clause 5.3; 05_order_form.md clause 1.6

Fee increase provisions conflict: MSA permits annual CPI-linked increases on 60 days' notice, while the Pricing and Rate Card says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or any increase. 01_msa.md clause 4.4; 10_pricing.md clause 1.3

Expense approval provisions conflict: SOW says expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval, while the Pricing and Rate Card requires prior approval only where expenses exceed £500 in a month. 02_sow.md clauses 5.2 and 5.4; 10_pricing.md clauses 3.1 and 3.2

Service level commencement conflicts: SOW applies platform service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md clause 7.1; 05_order_form.md clause 3.3
Availability target conflicts: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while the Service Level and Support Schedule requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md clause 7.2; 04_sla.md clause 3.1

Service credit cap conflicts: SOW permits credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps them at 10%, and the Pricing and Rate Card caps aggregate credits at 5%. 02_sow.md clause 7.4; 04_sla.md clause 4.2; 10_pricing.md clause 4.2

Support coverage conflicts: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and limited Business Day support for Priority 2 and 3, while the Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md clauses 2.1 and 2.2; 05_order_form.md clause 3.1

Business Day is defined three inconsistent ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays, and Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md clause 1.2; 04_sla.md clause 1.1; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Business Day

Response and Resolution targets are internally defective because times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response target effectively run from the response itself and allowing delay before acknowledgement. 04_sla.md clause 5.4

Security Incident is defined inconsistently: DPA covers any unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access causing loss or corruption; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md clause 1.6; 04_sla.md clause 7.1; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Security Incident

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of awareness, Information Security Policy within 48 hours of confirmation, and SLA within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md clause 6.1; 06_infosec.md clause 6.1; 04_sla.md clause 7.3
SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the Data Processing Addendum, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md clause 7.4; 03_dpa.md annexes

Acceptance criteria reference is wrong: MSA says Customer assesses Deliverables against Schedule 1, Section 12, but the SOW has no Section 12; acceptance criteria are in Exhibit A. 01_msa.md clause 6.2; 02_sow.md; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md

Acceptance process conflicts: MSA requires express written acceptance, SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days' silence, and Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and requires a signed acceptance certificate after a 15 Business Day review. 01_msa.md clause 6.1; 02_sow.md clause 6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 5.2 and 5.3

Deliverable source conflicts: SOW says deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of Deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md clause 6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 1.2 and 2

Deliverable warranty period conflicts: MSA warrants Deliverables for 90 days after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives a 180-day warranty for Material Defects. 01_msa.md clause 8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clause 7.1

Deliverable definition conflicts: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a Statement of Work, while the Glossary defines Deliverable as any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md clause 1.3; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Deliverable

Fee definition conflicts: MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under clause 4, while the Glossary defines Fee as all amounts payable under the Agreement, including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md clause 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Fee

Services definition conflicts: MSA defines Services only as services described in a SOW, while the Glossary adds support services described in the Service Level and Support Schedule. 01_msa.md clause 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Services

Confidential Information definition conflicts: MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing when disclosed, DPA makes all Customer Personal Data confidential whether marked or not, and the Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or oral/written. 01_msa.md clause 11.1; 03_dpa.md clause 1.4; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Confidential Information

Subprocessor definition conflicts: DPA limits Subprocessors to third parties processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to third parties processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md clause 1.5; 15_glossary.md section 2 definition of Subprocessor

Subcontracting/subprocessor consent conflicts: MSA permits subcontracting without Customer consent, DPA requires prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, and the Approved Subprocessor List allows additions/replacements on notice and objection rights. 01_msa.md clause 9.3; 03_dpa.md clause 5.1; 12_subprocessors.md clauses 3.1 to 3.4

Processing location conflicts: DPA allows Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and approved locations London/Dublin, while the SOW places the delivery team in Bengaluru, India, and the Information Security Policy allows any Provider region chosen by Provider's CISO. 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1 to 4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md clause 3.4; 06_infosec.md clause 2.1

Disaster recovery location is not an approved DPA processing location: BCDR uses Frankfurt, Germany, but DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations. 07_bcdr.md clause 3.1; 03_dpa.md clause 4.3 and Annex 2

Approved Subprocessor List includes a Singapore subprocessor, which conflicts with the DPA restriction against transfers outside the UK/EEA without prior written authorisation and an appropriate transfer mechanism. 12_subprocessors.md section 2 and clause 5.1; 03_dpa.md clauses 4.1 and 4.2

Approved Subprocessor List is mislabeled as Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already contains Annex 2 as the approved processing locations, not subprocessors. 12_subprocessors.md preamble; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

Data return/deletion obligations conflict: DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination, while Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days and handover by the end of a transition period extending six months after termination. 03_dpa.md clause 8.2; 09_exit.md clauses 2.1, 2.3, 4.1 and 5.2
Exit Plan refers to Data Processing Addendum clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md clause 5.3; 03_dpa.md

Records/data retention obligations conflict: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry/termination, while the DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days and the Exit Plan requires deletion after the 90-day retention/handover period. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 03_dpa.md clause 8.2; 09_exit.md clauses 2.3 and 5.2

Log/report retention obligations conflict with the MSA's 7-year retention requirement: Information Security Policy deletes security logs after 18 months, SLA retains service reports only for the duration of the Agreement, and Change Control retains the change log only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md clause 12.4; 06_infosec.md clause 5.2; 04_sla.md clause 6.3; 08_change_control.md clause 9.3

Audit rights conflict: MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/access rights beyond receiving SOC 2 Type II reports, while DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md clause 10.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 9.1 and 9.2

MSA records access clause is internally unclear because records must be made available on reasonable request 'in accordance with clause 10.2', but clause 10.2 denies any audit, inspection or premises/systems access beyond SOC 2 reporting. 01_msa.md clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Liability cap conflicts: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, SOW caps liability at £250,000, and DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3; 02_sow.md clause 9.2; 03_dpa.md clause 11.1

DPA indemnity for fines conflicts with the MSA liability cap and the MSA statement that the cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule or Addendum. 03_dpa.md clause 11.2; 01_msa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.3
Insurance requirement conflicts: MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md clause 16.1; 02_sow.md clause 9.4

Governing law conflicts: MSA applies England and Wales law and exclusive English/Welsh jurisdiction, while the DPA says it is governed by Irish law. 01_msa.md clauses 15.1 and 15.2; 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.2

DPA governing-law clause is internally inconsistent/redundant: clause 13.1 says the Addendum is governed by the Agreement's law except as clause 13.2 provides, while clause 13.2 then governs the entire Addendum by Irish law. 03_dpa.md clauses 13.1 and 13.2

Change approval process conflicts with MSA requirement that any change to Services be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation; Change Control allows deemed approval by Customer silence, unilateral approval by Provider's Delivery Lead up to £35,000, and emergency changes without prior approval. 01_msa.md clause 2.4; 08_change_control.md clauses 4.2, 4.3 and 6.1
Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17 and no Change Control Board. 08_change_control.md clause 4.1; 01_msa.md

Change Control Procedure allows Provider's Delivery Lead to approve changes costing up to £35,000 without Customer, conflicting with requirements elsewhere for Customer prior written approval for changes/expenses. 08_change_control.md clause 4.3; 01_msa.md clause 2.4; 02_sow.md clause 5.4

Rejected-change fee reference is defective: Change Control says Provider may charge for impact assessments for rejected Change Requests at the rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md clause 7.2; 09_exit.md clause 3.2

Escalation paths conflict: SOW escalation is delivery lead, account director, executive sponsor; Change Control escalation is Delivery Lead, Programme Director, Chief Information Officer. 02_sow.md clause 8.3; 08_change_control.md clause 8.1

Key personnel substitution conflicts: SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B allows substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md clause 3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md clauses 2.1 and 2.4

Team location conflicts: SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B locates the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md clause 3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md section 1
Named Key Personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says the individuals are named in a programme initiation document that is not included. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md clause 1.1

Exhibit A acceptance criteria depend on external materials not included in the contract set, such as the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md clauses 3.2 and 3.3

Information Security Policy refers to a quarterly security review, but no quarterly security review process is otherwise established; the SOW has a quarterly steering committee, not a security review. 06_infosec.md clause 6.3; 02_sow.md clause 8.2

Acceptable Use Policy permits unilateral amendment by Provider on 30 days' notice with acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA and Change Control requirement for written agreement/change control for changes to Services or contract terms. 11_acceptable_use.md clause 8.1; 01_msa.md clause 2.4; 08_change_control.md section 4

Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to disclose Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without notice where Provider considers it required, while MSA confidentiality allows disclosure only to personnel who need to know and contains no compelled-disclosure exception. 11_acceptable_use.md clause 6.1; 01_msa.md clause 11.2
