findings: The contract set contains inconsistent order-of-precedence provisions: the MSA says the MSA prevails over Schedules/Addenda, the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says it prevails over all documents and ranks Addenda below Schedules, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over any other document. This creates circular/incompatible precedence. MSA clause 14.2; SOW clause 1.2; Order Form clauses 2.1-2.2; Glossary clause 1.2

The Order Form is expressed to be under the MSA, but the MSA definition of Agreement includes only the MSA, Schedules and Addenda, not Order Forms. The Order Form’s contractual status is therefore inconsistent/unclear. MSA clause 1.1; Order Form heading and clause 2.1

The initial term is stated inconsistently: the MSA has a 24-month initial term, the SOW requires a 36-month programme, and the Order Form has a 12-month initial term. MSA clause 3.1; SOW clause 2.1; Order Form clause 1.2
The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form service commencement date. MSA Effective Date and clause 3.1; SOW clause 2.2; Order Form clauses 1.3 and 7.3

Convenience termination notice periods conflict: the MSA requires at least 90 days’ notice, the SOW requires 30 days’ notice for the SOW, and the Order Form permits non-renewal on 30 days’ notice. MSA clause 3.3; SOW clause 2.3; Order Form clause 6.2

The MSA renewal mechanism requires termination under clause 3.3, while the Order Form has a separate non-renewal regime. The two renewal/notice regimes are not aligned. MSA clauses 3.2-3.3; Order Form clauses 6.1-6.2

The monthly recurring charge/Fee is stated four different ways: £12,400 in the MSA, £12,800 in the SOW, £12,800 implied by the Order Form annual contract value, and £13,100 in the Pricing Schedule. MSA clause 4.1; SOW clause 5.1; Order Form clause 1.4; Pricing Schedule clause 1.1

Invoicing timing conflicts: the MSA, SOW and Order Form provide for monthly invoicing in arrears, while the Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is invoiced monthly in advance. MSA clause 4.3; SOW clause 5.3; Order Form clause 1.5; Pricing Schedule clauses 1.2 and 6.1
Payment terms conflict: 30 days from receipt, 45 days from receipt, and 60 days from invoice date are all specified. MSA clause 4.3; SOW clause 5.3; Order Form clause 1.6

The MSA permits annual CPI-linked Fee increases on 60 days’ notice, while the Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed during the initial term and not subject to indexation or increase. MSA clause 4.4; Pricing Schedule clause 1.3

Expense recovery conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers travel unless expressly stated otherwise and that expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel/subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. SOW clauses 5.2 and 5.4; Pricing Schedule clauses 3.1-3.2

The MSA says no Deliverable is accepted unless Customer expressly accepts in writing, while the SOW says Deliverables are deemed accepted after 5 Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and requires a signed acceptance certificate. MSA clause 6.1; SOW clause 6.3; Exhibit A clauses 5.2-5.3

The acceptance review period conflicts: the SOW gives Customer 5 Business Days before deemed acceptance, while Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days to assess a Deliverable. SOW clause 6.3; Exhibit A clause 5.2

The resubmission/remediation period conflicts: the SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments, while Exhibit A gives a further 15-Business-Day assessment period after remedy and resubmission without matching the SOW process. SOW clause 6.4; Exhibit A clause 5.4
The MSA refers to acceptance criteria in Schedule 1, Section 12, but Schedule 1/SOW has no Section 12. MSA clause 6.2; SOW

The source of Deliverables conflicts: the SOW says Deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A lists the Deliverables and says it is the sole source of acceptance criteria. SOW clause 6.1; Exhibit A clauses 1.2 and 2
Deliverable warranty periods conflict: the MSA provides a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A provides 180 days. MSA clause 8.2; Exhibit A clause 7.1
The acceptance criteria depend on documents not included in the contract set, such as the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. Exhibit A clauses 3.2-3.3

Business Day is defined three different ways: Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays, Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays, and Monday-Friday including public holidays. MSA clause 1.2; SLA clause 1.1; Glossary section 2

Confidential Information is defined inconsistently: the MSA covers only information marked confidential in writing, the DPA treats all Customer Personal Data as Confidential Information whether marked or not, and the Glossary covers all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement whether marked or oral/written. MSA clause 11.1; DPA clause 1.4; Glossary section 2

Deliverable is defined inconsistently: the MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while the Glossary includes any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. MSA clause 1.3; Glossary section 2

Fee is defined inconsistently: the MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while the Glossary includes all amounts payable under the Agreement, including recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. MSA clause 1.4; Glossary section 2
Services is defined inconsistently: the MSA limits Services to those described in a SOW, while the Glossary also includes support services described in the SLA. MSA clause 1.5; Glossary section 2
Security Incident is defined inconsistently across the DPA, SLA and Glossary, with materially different thresholds and scope. DPA clause 1.6; SLA clause 7.1; Glossary section 2

Security incident notification deadlines conflict: 24 hours from awareness under the DPA, 72 hours from confirmation under the SLA, and 48 hours from confirmation under the Information Security Policy. DPA clause 6.1; SLA clause 7.3; Information Security Policy clause 6.1

The SLA’s Security Incident definition is narrower than the DPA’s definition and would omit incidents covered by the DPA, such as mere unauthorised access or disclosure without confirmed loss/corruption. DPA clause 1.6; SLA clause 7.1
The SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. SLA clause 7.4; DPA annexes
Availability service levels conflict: the SOW requires 99.5%, while the SLA requires 99.9%. SOW clause 7.2; SLA clause 3.1

The start date for service levels conflicts: the SOW applies service levels from the start of Phase 3, while the Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date. SOW clause 7.1; Order Form clause 3.3

Support coverage conflicts: the SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and limited Business Day support for Priority 2 and Priority 3, while the Order Form says support is 24x7 for all priority levels. SLA clauses 2.1-2.2; Order Form clause 3.1

Service credit caps conflict: the SOW allows credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, the SLA caps them at 10%, and the Pricing Schedule caps aggregate credits at 5%. SOW clause 7.4; SLA clause 4.2; Pricing Schedule clause 4.2

The SLA says service credits are the sole financial remedy for availability failures, but other documents preserve broader liability/remedies and different caps, creating remedial inconsistency. SLA clause 4.3; MSA clause 13; DPA clause 11; Pricing Schedule clause 4

The SLA measures response and resolution times from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time obligation circular because the response clock starts only after Provider has responded/acknowledged. SLA clause 5.4

BCDR suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event and excludes related unavailability from availability calculations, while the SLA contains no matching exclusion except maintenance, Customer network/equipment and certain third-party causes. BCDR clauses 5.1-5.3; SLA clauses 3.2-3.3 and 9

BCDR allows an 8-hour RTO after Invocation and gives no deadline for Invocation, conflicting with the SLA Priority 1 resolution target of 4 hours for total platform unavailability. BCDR clauses 1.5, 2.1 and 4.1; SLA clause 5.1
Professional indemnity insurance limits conflict: the MSA requires at least £5,000,000, while the SOW requires at least £2,000,000. MSA clause 16.1; SOW clause 9.4

Liability caps conflict: the MSA caps liability at 12 months’ Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding Schedules/Addenda, the SOW caps Provider’s liability at £250,000, and the DPA disapplies all limitations for DPA/Data Protection Law breaches. MSA clauses 13.1 and 13.3; SOW clause 9.2; DPA clause 11.1
The DPA indemnity for fines may be uncapped under the DPA, but the MSA purports to cap liability notwithstanding any Addendum, creating a direct conflict. MSA clause 13.3; DPA clause 11.2

Audit rights conflict: the MSA says Customer has no audit/inspection/right to attend Provider premises or systems beyond receiving the SOC 2 report, while the DPA permits annual audits including premises, systems and records. MSA clause 10.2; DPA clauses 9.1-9.2

Records access is internally conflicted because the MSA requires Provider to make records available on reasonable request but only in accordance with clause 10.2, which denies further audit/inspection rights. MSA clauses 10.2 and 12.2

Record/data retention obligations conflict: the MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, the DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days, the Exit Plan requires 90-day retention of Customer data, the Information Security Policy requires deletion of logs after 18 months, and the SLA keeps service reports only for the Agreement duration. MSA clause 12.4; DPA clause 8.2; Exit Plan clause 2.3; Information Security Policy clause 5.2; SLA clause 6.3

The DPA deletion obligation within 30 days after expiry/termination conflicts with the Exit Plan’s requirement to continue Services through a transition period ending 6 months after termination and to retain Customer data for transition. DPA clause 8.2; Exit Plan clauses 2.1-2.3 and 4.1(a)

The Exit Plan is internally inconsistent because it requires Provider to retain Customer data for only 90 days after termination, but the transition period runs until 6 months after termination and Provider must provide Services and deliver data through that period. Exit Plan clauses 2.1-2.3 and 4.1(a)
The Exit Plan refers to personal data obligations in DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. Exit Plan clause 5.3; DPA
The Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. Change Control Procedure clause 4.1; MSA

The Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval if Customer does not respond, conflicting with the MSA requirement that changes be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation. MSA clause 2.4; Change Control Procedure clause 4.2

The Change Control Procedure allows Provider’s Delivery Lead to approve changes up to £35,000 without Customer involvement, conflicting with the MSA requirement for written agreement by both parties to changes. MSA clause 2.4; Change Control Procedure clause 4.3

The Change Control Procedure allows emergency changes without prior approval, conflicting with the MSA requirement that any change be agreed in writing before implementation. MSA clause 2.4; Change Control Procedure clause 6.1

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for rejected-change impact assessments at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not state a rate for impact assessments. Change Control Procedure clause 7.2; Exit Plan

The MSA allows Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without Customer’s prior consent, conflicting with the DPA’s specific prior-consent requirement for Subprocessors processing Customer Personal Data. MSA clause 9.3; DPA clause 5.1

Governing law conflicts: the MSA applies England and Wales law and exclusive English/Welsh jurisdiction, while the DPA says the DPA and disputes arising out of it are governed by Irish law. MSA clauses 15.1-15.2; DPA clauses 13.1-13.2

The DPA governing-law provision is internally awkward because clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the Agreement law save as provided in clause 13.2, while clause 13.2 then applies Irish law to the whole DPA and any dispute arising out of it. DPA clauses 13.1-13.2

The MSA confidentiality clause permits disclosure only to personnel who need to know, while the Acceptable Use Policy permits disclosure of Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without notice where Provider considers it required. MSA clause 11.2; Acceptable Use Policy clauses 6.1-6.2

The Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the policy on 30 days’ notice with acceptance deemed by continued use, conflicting with the MSA and Change Control Procedure framework requiring agreed change control for changes to the Services/contract terms. MSA clause 2.4; Change Control Procedure section 4; Acceptable Use Policy clauses 8.1-8.2

The Information Security Policy refers to making the incident register available at the quarterly security review, but no quarterly security review is established in the contract set. Information Security Policy clause 6.3

The Pricing Schedule uses the Service Commencement Date and initial term, but the MSA does not define Service Commencement Date and the contract set contains conflicting initial terms. Pricing Schedule clauses 1.3 and 7.1; MSA clause 3.1; Order Form clauses 1.2-1.3

The Purchase Order provisions allow invoices without a valid PO number to be returned unpaid, while the main payment clauses require payment of undisputed invoices within specified periods and do not make PO-number inclusion a condition to payment. Order Form clauses 5.2-5.3; MSA clause 4.3; SOW clause 5.3

The Glossary’s definition of Agreement includes Exhibits entered into under the Order Form/MSA, while the MSA definition of Agreement does not include Exhibits. This affects whether Exhibit A and Exhibit B are part of the Agreement. MSA clause 1.1; Glossary section 2; Exhibits A and B headings

The Glossary definition of Subprocessor covers third parties processing Personal Data generally, while the DPA definition is limited to third parties processing Customer Personal Data. This could expand the term beyond the DPA scope. DPA clause 1.5; Glossary section 2
unmatched: The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form service commencement date. MSA Effective Date and clause 3.1; SOW clause 2.2; Order Form clauses 1.3 and 7.3

The MSA renewal mechanism requires termination under clause 3.3, while the Order Form has a separate non-renewal regime. The two renewal/notice regimes are not aligned. MSA clauses 3.2-3.3; Order Form clauses 6.1-6.2

Expense recovery conflicts: the SOW says the Fee covers travel unless expressly stated otherwise and that expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval, while the Pricing Schedule makes travel/subsistence recoverable at cost and requires prior approval only above £500 per month. SOW clauses 5.2 and 5.4; Pricing Schedule clauses 3.1-3.2

The resubmission/remediation period conflicts: the SOW requires resubmission within 10 Business Days after comments, while Exhibit A gives a further 15-Business-Day assessment period after remedy and resubmission without matching the SOW process. SOW clause 6.4; Exhibit A clause 5.4

The SLA says service credits are the sole financial remedy for availability failures, but other documents preserve broader liability/remedies and different caps, creating remedial inconsistency. SLA clause 4.3; MSA clause 13; DPA clause 11; Pricing Schedule clause 4

The SLA measures response and resolution times from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time obligation circular because the response clock starts only after Provider has responded/acknowledged. SLA clause 5.4

The Change Control Procedure allows emergency changes without prior approval, conflicting with the MSA requirement that any change be agreed in writing before implementation. MSA clause 2.4; Change Control Procedure clause 6.1

The Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for rejected-change impact assessments at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit and Transition Plan does not state a rate for impact assessments. Change Control Procedure clause 7.2; Exit Plan

The SOW refers to named key personnel, but the names are not included in the contract set; Exhibit B says they are in a programme initiation document that is not provided. SOW clause 3.5; Exhibit B clause 1.1

The DPA governing-law provision is internally awkward because clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the Agreement law save as provided in clause 13.2, while clause 13.2 then applies Irish law to the whole DPA and any dispute arising out of it. DPA clauses 13.1-13.2

Order Form clauses 5.2-5.3; MSA clause 4.3; SOW clause 5.3

The term “Security Incident” is defined inconsistently: DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access to Customer data resulting in loss or corruption; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 15_glossary.md §2

The term “Subprocessor” is defined inconsistently: DPA limits it to a third party processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to a third party processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

The MSA starts on 1 April 2027, but the SOW programme commences on 1 March 2027, before the MSA effective date and before the Order Form signature date of 12 March 2027. 01_msa.md Effective Date; 02_sow.md §2.2; 05_order_form.md §7.3

The initial term is inconsistent: MSA initial term is 24 months, SOW programme duration is 36 months, and Order Form initial term is 12 months from 1 April 2027. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §§1.2-1.3

Renewal and non-renewal/termination mechanics conflict: MSA renews after a 24-month initial term and allows convenience termination on 90 days’ notice, while the Order Form renews after 12-month periods unless non-renewal notice is given 30 days before term end. 01_msa.md §§3.1-3.3; 05_order_form.md §§6.1-6.2
Convenience termination notice differs: MSA requires at least 90 days’ written notice, while SOW permits termination of the SOW on 30 days’ notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3

Monthly charges conflict: MSA says £12,400 per month; SOW says £12,800; Pricing Schedule says £13,100; Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 implies £12,800 per month. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Billing timing conflicts: MSA and SOW require monthly invoicing in arrears, while the Pricing Schedule requires the recurring charge to be invoiced monthly in advance. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 10_pricing.md §1.2

Payment terms conflict: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW within 45 days of receipt, and Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Price increase/indexation terms conflict: MSA allows annual CPI-linked increases on 60 days’ notice, while the Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Expense recovery terms conflict: SOW says the Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel unless expressly stated otherwise and expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval; Pricing Schedule says travel and subsistence are recoverable at cost and need prior approval only above £500 per month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

The Order Form allows invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the general obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the contractual payment period. 01_msa.md §4.3; 05_order_form.md §§5.2-5.3

Acceptance provisions conflict: MSA requires express written acceptance; SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence; Exhibit A says silence does not constitute acceptance and requires a signed acceptance certificate after a 15 Business Day review period. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§5.2-5.3
MSA refers Customer assessment to “Schedule 1, Section 12,” but the SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Sources of deliverables and acceptance criteria conflict: SOW says deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A lists specific deliverables and says it is the sole source of acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2, 3
Acceptance criteria rely on documents not included in the contract set, including the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3

Deliverable warranty period conflicts: MSA gives a 90-day warranty following acceptance, while Exhibit A gives a 180-day warranty for accepted Deliverables. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Provider audit rights conflict: MSA says Customer has no right beyond receiving the annual SOC 2 Type II report and no right to audit/inspect/attend premises or systems; DPA grants annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records; Information Security Policy also requires sharing penetration test reports and making an incident register available at quarterly security review. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2; 06_infosec.md §§6.3, 7.2

MSA record-access clause is internally inconsistent because it says Provider shall make records available on reasonable request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 denies any audit/inspection right beyond the SOC 2 report. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Record/data retention obligations conflict: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination; DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days; Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days and then deletion. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2

Security log retention conflicts with the MSA’s 7-year retention requirement: Information Security Policy requires security logs to be retained for 18 months and then deleted. 01_msa.md §12.4; 06_infosec.md §5.2
Service report retention conflicts with the MSA’s 7-year record retention requirement: SLA requires reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md §12.4; 04_sla.md §6.3

Liability provisions conflict: MSA caps aggregate liability at 12 months’ fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum; SOW caps liability at £250,000; DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to DPA/Data Protection Law breaches and includes an indemnity for fines. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2; 03_dpa.md §§11.1-11.2
Insurance requirements conflict: MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Processing-location obligations conflict: DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and approved locations London/Dublin; SOW states the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India; Exhibit B locates key personnel in Bengaluru; Information Security Policy allows any Provider region selected by Provider’s CISO. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1; 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3

BCDR recovery site is Frankfurt, Germany, but DPA Annex 2 lists only London and Dublin as approved processing locations; if Customer Personal Data is replicated to Frankfurt, it is not listed as approved. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 07_bcdr.md §§3.1-3.3

Approved Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics in Singapore, outside the UK/EEA approved processing territory and outside the DPA Annex 2 approved locations. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md §2

Subprocessor approval process conflicts: DPA requires Customer’s prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Approved Subprocessor List permits Provider to add/replace Subprocessors on notice, proceed after unresolved objection, and make immediate replacements with notice afterwards. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

MSA subcontracting right conflicts with DPA Subprocessor consent requirement: MSA allows subcontracting any part of the Services without Customer consent, while DPA requires prior written consent for each Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

Document 12 is labelled both Schedule 9 to the MSA and Annex 2 to the DPA, but the DPA already has an Annex 2 titled Approved Processing Locations; the two Annex 2s have different content. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md heading and introductory text

Security Incident notification deadlines conflict: DPA requires notice within 24 hours of becoming aware; Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation; SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirming a narrower category of Security Incident. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1
SLA refers to escalation contacts in Annex 3 of the DPA, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md

Governing law conflicts: MSA selects England and Wales law and exclusive English/Welsh courts; DPA clause 13.2 selects Republic of Ireland law for the DPA and disputes arising out of it. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

DPA clause 13 is internally inconsistent because clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the Agreement’s law except as provided in 13.2, while 13.2 then applies Irish law to the entire DPA and disputes arising out of it. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

Support coverage conflicts: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and limited Business Day hours for Priority 2/3, while the Order Form states 24x7 coverage for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1
Availability level conflicts: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md §7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Date from which service levels apply conflicts: SOW says platform service levels apply from the start of Phase 3; Order Form says service levels apply from the Service Commencement Date of 1 April 2027. 02_sow.md §7.1; 05_order_form.md §§1.3, 3.3

Service credit caps conflict: SOW allows credits up to 25% of monthly Fee; SLA caps monthly credits at 10%; Pricing Schedule caps aggregate credits at 5% of the recurring monthly charge. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2; 10_pricing.md §4.2

Service credit remedy provisions conflict with liability/remedy structure: SLA says service credits are Customer’s sole financial remedy for availability failures, while other documents contain broader liability, indemnity and service-credit provisions without the same limitation. 01_msa.md §13; 03_dpa.md §11; 04_sla.md §4.3; 10_pricing.md §4

SLA response-time measurement is defective because response and resolution times are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response target measured from the response itself rather than from report/detection of the Incident. 04_sla.md §5.4

BCDR recovery objectives conflict with SLA Priority 1 targets for total unavailability: SLA requires Resolution within 4 hours, while BCDR permits an 8-hour RTO after Invocation and suspends SLA obligations during a Continuity Event. 04_sla.md §5.1; 07_bcdr.md §§2.1, 5.1

BCDR excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations, but SLA availability exclusions do not expressly include Continuity Events, creating inconsistent availability-credit treatment. 04_sla.md §§3.2-3.3, 9; 07_bcdr.md §§5.1-5.3
BCDR references a dependency list to be reviewed at each annual test, but no dependency list is included in the Plan or contract set. 07_bcdr.md §8.3
Change Control Procedure refers to a Change Control Board described in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md §4.1; 01_msa.md

Change approval mechanics conflict with MSA clause 2.4: MSA requires any Services change to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation; Change Control allows deemed approval by silence, unilateral approval by Provider’s Delivery Lead for changes up to £35,000, and emergency implementation without prior approval. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §§4.2-4.4, 6.1-6.3

Provider’s Delivery Lead may unilaterally approve changes up to £35,000, conflicting with Customer approval/payment-control provisions and potentially imposing charges without Customer’s written agreement. 01_msa.md §§2.4, 4.5; 08_change_control.md §§4.3, 5.1

Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

Change escalation path conflicts with SOW governance escalation: SOW escalates delivery lead → account director → executive sponsor; Change Control escalates Delivery Lead → Programme Director → Chief Information Officer. 02_sow.md §8.3; 08_change_control.md §§8.1-8.2

Team location provisions conflict: SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, India, while Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London and only some key roles in Bengaluru. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Key-personnel substitution rules conflict: SOW prohibits substituting named key personnel without Customer’s prior written agreement; Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days’ notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances without prior agreement. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1-2.4

Named key personnel are not actually named in the contract set; Exhibit B says the individuals are named in the programme initiation document, which is not provided. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1

Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the Policy on 30 days’ notice with acceptance by continued use, conflicting with the MSA requirement for written agreement to changes and the Change Control Procedure for changes to Services/terms. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §1.1; 11_acceptable_use.md §§8.1-8.2

AUP suspension can make Services unavailable while charges continue, but SLA availability exclusions do not expressly exclude Provider suspensions for alleged AUP breaches, creating uncertainty over service credits during suspension. 04_sla.md §§3, 9; 11_acceptable_use.md §§5.1-5.4

AUP allows disclosure of Customer content to law enforcement/regulators without notice, while DPA requires processing only on documented instructions and imposes stricter controls for Customer Personal Data; the documents do not reconcile lawful-disclosure exceptions with DPA obligations. 03_dpa.md §§2.2, 6.3; 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2
Exit Plan says Provider’s personal-data obligations are in DPA clause 14, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md

Exit Plan applies on expiry as well as termination, but defines the transition period as beginning when notice of termination is given; it does not define when the transition period begins if the Agreement simply expires or is not renewed. 09_exit.md §§1.1-1.2, 2.1

Exit Plan transition timing is internally inconsistent: the transition period runs until six months after termination, but Provider retains Customer data for only 90 days following termination to support transition, which may end before the transition period ends. 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

DPA requires deletion of Customer Personal Data within 30 days after expiry/termination, while Exit Plan requires return/handover by the end of a six-month post-termination transition period and retention for 90 days, so both cannot be satisfied for personal data without further qualification. 03_dpa.md §8.2; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3, 4.1, 5.1-5.2

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but Exit Plan requires Provider to continue Services and process/retain Customer data during a post-termination transition period, creating uncertainty whether post-termination processing is authorised. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

Exit Plan requires delivery of all Deliverables including source code and build scripts on exit, while MSA assigns IP in Deliverables only on payment in full, creating uncertainty if exit occurs before full payment. 01_msa.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §4.1(b)

Transition assistance rate conflicts with rate-card provisions: Exit Plan sets £1,250 per person per day, while Pricing Schedule sets a standard £1,450 per person per day unless Exhibit B role-specific rates apply. 09_exit.md §3.2; 10_pricing.md §2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3

Pricing Schedule’s recurring charge and volume overage regime is not reconciled with SOW’s statement that the monthly Fee covers all personnel, tooling and travel; the documents do not state whether volume charges are included in or additional to the Fee. 02_sow.md §§5.1-5.2; 10_pricing.md §§1.1, 5.1-5.2

Service credits are to be deducted from invoices, but MSA requires Customer to pay all amounts in full without set-off, deduction or withholding except as required by law or agreed by Provider in writing; the documents do not reconcile automatic credits with the no-deduction clause. 01_msa.md §4.5; 04_sla.md §4.1; 10_pricing.md §4.1

The Approved Subprocessor List allows Provider to maintain and publish the current version on its trust portal, but DPA requires prior written consent to specific Subprocessors; a mutable portal list is not reconciled with specific prior consent. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§1.2, 3.1-3.4

Information Security Policy allows Customer data in any Provider region determined by Provider, with notice of new regions only after entry into service, conflicting with DPA’s prior written authorisation requirement for transfers outside the UK/EEA and Annex 2 location restrictions. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3; 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3

Security controls classify payment card data as Restricted Data, but the Acceptable Use Policy prohibits Customer from storing payment card primary account numbers on the platform; the documents do not clarify what payment card data may be processed despite the prohibition. 06_infosec.md §1.2; 11_acceptable_use.md §3.2
unmatched: The prompt says the set consists of four documents, but the materials contain fifteen contract documents, creating uncertainty as to the contract set under review. Document list / headings of Documents 01-15

The term “Deliverable” is defined differently: MSA limits it to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while the Glossary includes any output whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md §1.3; 15_glossary.md §2

The term “Subprocessor” is defined inconsistently: DPA limits it to a third party processing Customer Personal Data, while the Glossary refers to a third party processing Personal Data generally. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

The Order Form allows invoices without a valid purchase order number to be returned unpaid, conflicting with the general obligation to pay undisputed invoices within the contractual payment period. 01_msa.md §4.3; 05_order_form.md §§5.2-5.3
Acceptance criteria rely on documents not included in the contract set, including the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3
Service report retention conflicts with the MSA’s 7-year record retention requirement: SLA requires reports to be retained only for the duration of the Agreement. 01_msa.md §12.4; 04_sla.md §6.3

DPA clause 13 is internally inconsistent because clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the Agreement’s law except as provided in 13.2, while 13.2 then applies Irish law to the entire DPA and disputes arising out of it. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

SLA response-time measurement is defective because response and resolution times are measured from Provider’s acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response target measured from the response itself rather than from report/detection of the Incident. 04_sla.md §5.4
BCDR references a dependency list to be reviewed at each annual test, but no dependency list is included in the Plan or contract set. 07_bcdr.md §8.3

Change Control Procedure says Provider may charge for preparing an impact assessment for a rejected Change Request at the rate set out in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan does not set a specific impact-assessment rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

DPA Annex 1 says processing duration is the term of the Agreement, but Exit Plan requires Provider to continue Services and process/retain Customer data during a post-termination transition period, creating uncertainty whether post-termination processing is authorised. 03_dpa.md Annex 1; 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3

findings: Circular/inconsistent precedence: the MSA says the MSA prevails over every Schedule/Addendum, while the SOW says the SOW prevails over the MSA, the Order Form says the Order Form prevails over all documents and ranks Addenda below Schedules, and the Glossary says its definitions prevail over all other definitions despite being only a Schedule. 01_msa.md §§14.1-14.2; 02_sow.md §§1.1-1.2; 05_order_form.md §§2.1-2.2; 15_glossary.md §1.2
The SOW programme commences before the MSA effective date, although the SOW is issued under the MSA. 01_msa.md Effective Date and §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.2
Conflicting initial terms/durations: MSA initial term is 24 months, SOW programme is 36 months, and Order Form initial term is 12 months. 01_msa.md §3.1; 02_sow.md §2.1; 05_order_form.md §1.2
Conflicting termination-for-convenience notice periods: MSA requires at least 90 days' notice, while SOW permits termination on 30 days' notice. 01_msa.md §3.3; 02_sow.md §2.3

Renewal/non-renewal mechanics conflict: MSA renews unless terminated under a 90-day termination provision, while the Order Form renews unless 30 days' non-renewal notice is given. 01_msa.md §§3.2-3.3; 05_order_form.md §§6.1-6.2

Conflicting monthly recurring charges: MSA states £12,400, SOW states £12,800, Pricing Schedule states £13,100, and Order Form annual contract value implies £12,800 per month. 01_msa.md §4.1; 02_sow.md §5.1; 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1
Order Form annual contract value of £153,600 is inconsistent with the Pricing Schedule monthly recurring charge of £13,100, which totals £157,200 annually. 05_order_form.md §1.4; 10_pricing.md §1.1

Conflicting invoicing timing: MSA and SOW require monthly invoicing in arrears, while Pricing Schedule requires monthly invoicing in advance on the first Business Day. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 10_pricing.md §§1.2, 6.1

Conflicting payment terms: MSA requires payment within 30 days of receipt, SOW within 45 days of receipt, and Order Form within 60 days from invoice date. 01_msa.md §4.3; 02_sow.md §5.3; 05_order_form.md §1.6

Conflicting price increase rules: MSA permits annual CPI-linked increases on 60 days' notice, while Pricing Schedule says the recurring charge is fixed for the initial term and not subject to indexation or other increase. 01_msa.md §4.4; 10_pricing.md §1.3

Conflicting expense recovery rules: SOW says the Fee covers travel and expenses outside the Fee require prior written approval, while Pricing Schedule says travel and subsistence are recoverable at cost and only require prior approval above £500 per month. 02_sow.md §§5.2, 5.4; 10_pricing.md §§3.1-3.2

Conflicting definitions of Business Day: MSA uses Monday-Friday excluding England and Wales public holidays; SLA uses Monday-Saturday excluding US federal holidays; Glossary uses Monday-Friday including public holidays. 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Agreement: MSA includes the MSA plus Schedules/Addenda executed under it, while Glossary also includes the Order Form and Exhibits entered into under any of them. 01_msa.md §1.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Deliverable: MSA limits Deliverables to items identified as deliverables in a SOW, while Glossary covers any output of the Services whether or not identified in a SOW. 01_msa.md §1.3; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting definitions of Fee: MSA defines Fee as amounts payable under MSA clause 4, while Glossary includes all recurring charges, time-and-materials charges and expenses. 01_msa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2
Conflicting definitions of Services: MSA defines Services as those described in a SOW, while Glossary also includes support services under the SLA Schedule. 01_msa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting confidentiality scope: MSA protects only information marked confidential in writing at disclosure, DPA treats all Customer Personal Data as Confidential Information whether marked or not, and Glossary treats all information disclosed in connection with the Agreement as confidential whether marked or not and whether oral or written. 01_msa.md §11.1; 03_dpa.md §1.4; 15_glossary.md §2
MSA cross-reference is defective: acceptance criteria are said to be in Schedule 1, Section 12, but SOW/Schedule 1 has no Section 12. 01_msa.md §6.2; 02_sow.md

Conflicting acceptance mechanisms: MSA requires express written acceptance and no deemed acceptance, SOW deems acceptance after 5 Business Days of silence, and Exhibit A gives Customer 15 Business Days and states silence does not constitute acceptance. 01_msa.md §6.1; 02_sow.md §6.3; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§5.2-5.3

Conflicting sources of deliverables/acceptance criteria: SOW says deliverables are listed in a phase plan maintained by the delivery lead, while Exhibit A says it is the sole source of deliverables and acceptance criteria. 02_sow.md §6.1; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§1.2, 2, 3
Exhibit A acceptance criteria rely on documents not included or defined in the contract set, including the requirements register and agreed functional test pack. 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §§3.2-3.3
Conflicting deliverable warranty periods: MSA gives a 90-day warranty after acceptance, while Exhibit A gives 180 days. 01_msa.md §8.2; 13_exhibit_a_acceptance.md §7.1

Conflicting team location requirements: SOW says the delivery team operates from Bengaluru, while Exhibit B places the Delivery Lead and Lead Solution Architect in London. 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1

Conflicting key personnel substitution rules: SOW prohibits substitution of named key personnel without Customer's prior written agreement, while Exhibit B permits substitution on 10 Business Days' notice and immediate substitution in specified circumstances. 02_sow.md §3.5; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §§2.1-2.4
Exhibit B refers to individuals named in a programme initiation document, but that document is not included in the contract set. 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1.1
Conflicting service-level start dates: SOW applies service levels from Phase 3, while Order Form applies service levels from the Service Commencement Date. 02_sow.md §7.1; 05_order_form.md §3.3
Conflicting availability commitments: SOW requires 99.5% monthly availability, while SLA requires 99.9%. 02_sow.md §7.2; 04_sla.md §3.1

Conflicting service credit caps: SOW allows service credits up to 25% of the monthly Fee, SLA caps them at 10%, and Pricing Schedule caps aggregate monthly service credits at 5%. 02_sow.md §7.4; 04_sla.md §4.2; 10_pricing.md §4.2

Conflicting support coverage: SLA provides 24x7 support only for Priority 1 and limited Business Day support for Priority 2 and 3, while Order Form states 24x7 support for all priority levels. 04_sla.md §§2.1-2.2; 05_order_form.md §3.1

SLA response and resolution times are measured from Provider's acknowledgement of the Incident, making the response-time target circular because acknowledgement is normally the response. 04_sla.md §5.4
SLA references Annex 3 of the DPA for Security Incident escalation contacts, but the DPA has no Annex 3. 04_sla.md §7.4; 03_dpa.md

Conflicting definitions of Security Incident: DPA covers unauthorised/unlawful access, acquisition, alteration, disclosure, loss or destruction of Customer Personal Data; SLA covers only confirmed unauthorised access causing loss or corruption; Information Security Policy covers confirmed incidents affecting Customer data; Glossary covers any event affecting confidentiality, integrity or availability of Customer data or the platform. 03_dpa.md §1.6; 04_sla.md §7.1; 06_infosec.md §6.1; 15_glossary.md §2

Conflicting Security Incident notification deadlines: DPA requires notice without undue delay and within 24 hours of awareness, Information Security Policy requires notice within 48 hours of confirmation, and SLA requires notice within 72 hours of confirmation. 03_dpa.md §6.1; 04_sla.md §7.3; 06_infosec.md §6.1

Conflicting data processing locations: DPA permits Customer Personal Data processing only in the UK/EEA and lists London and Dublin, while SOW/Exhibit B place delivery personnel in Bengaluru, Information Security Policy permits any Provider region determined by Provider, BCDR uses Frankfurt, and the Subprocessor List includes Singapore and Manchester. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 02_sow.md §3.4; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §1; 06_infosec.md §2.1; 07_bcdr.md §3.1; 12_subprocessors.md §2

DPA Annex 2 lists approved processing locations as London and Dublin, but the Approved Subprocessor List states that it is Annex 2 to the DPA and instead lists subprocessors and locations, creating duplicate/incompatible Annex 2 content. 03_dpa.md Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md introductory text and §2

The Subprocessor List includes Kestrel Analytics Pte Ltd in Singapore, which conflicts with the DPA restriction to the UK/EEA and DPA Annex 2 approved locations of London and Dublin. 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3 and Annex 2; 12_subprocessors.md §2

Conflicting subprocessor approval rules: DPA requires Customer's prior written consent to each specific Subprocessor, while the Subprocessor List permits additions/replacements on notice with an objection right and even immediate replacement with notice afterwards. 03_dpa.md §5.1; 12_subprocessors.md §§3.1-3.4

Conflicting subcontracting/subprocessing consent position: MSA permits Provider to subcontract any part of the Services without prior consent, while DPA requires prior written consent for any Subprocessor processing Customer Personal Data. 01_msa.md §9.3; 03_dpa.md §5.1

Conflicting audit rights: MSA states Customer has no audit, inspection or premises/systems access rights beyond receiving SOC 2, while DPA permits annual audits including inspection of premises, systems and records. 01_msa.md §10.2; 03_dpa.md §§9.1-9.2

MSA records clause is internally constrained by a conflicting cross-reference: Provider must make records available on request in accordance with clause 10.2, but clause 10.2 says Customer has no further right to audit, inspect or attend Provider premises or systems. 01_msa.md §§10.2, 12.2

Conflicting record/data retention and deletion duties: MSA requires Provider to retain all records, data and materials for 7 years after expiry/termination, DPA requires deletion of all Customer Personal Data within 30 days, Exit Plan requires retention of Customer data for 90 days and deletion only after retention and handover, and Information Security Policy requires security logs to be deleted after 18 months. 01_msa.md §12.4; 03_dpa.md §§8.2-8.3; 09_exit.md §§2.3, 5.2; 06_infosec.md §5.2

SLA service report retention for only the duration of the Agreement conflicts with the MSA requirement to retain records relating to the Agreement for 7 years after expiry or termination. 04_sla.md §6.3; 01_msa.md §12.4

Exit Plan says Provider must retain Customer data for transition after termination, while DPA requires Customer Personal Data to be deleted within 30 days of expiry/termination; both cannot be satisfied for personal data needed during the six-month transition period. 09_exit.md §§2.1-2.3, 5.2; 03_dpa.md §8.2
Exit Plan cross-reference is defective: it refers to DPA clause 14 for personal data obligations, but the DPA has no clause 14. 09_exit.md §5.3; 03_dpa.md

Conflicting liability caps: MSA caps each party's aggregate liability at 12 months' Fees and says that cap applies notwithstanding any Schedule/Addendum, SOW caps Provider liability at £250,000, and DPA says no limitation or exclusion applies to breaches of the DPA or Data Protection Law. 01_msa.md §§13.1, 13.3; 02_sow.md §9.2; 03_dpa.md §11.1
Conflicting insurance requirements: MSA requires professional indemnity insurance of at least £5,000,000, while SOW requires only £2,000,000. 01_msa.md §16.1; 02_sow.md §9.4

Conflicting governing law: MSA is governed by England and Wales law with exclusive England and Wales jurisdiction, while DPA states it is governed by the laws of the Republic of Ireland. 01_msa.md §§15.1-15.2; 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

DPA governing-law drafting is internally awkward: clause 13.1 says the DPA is governed by the law applicable to the Agreement save as clause 13.2, while clause 13.2 entirely replaces that law with Irish law for the DPA and disputes arising out of it. 03_dpa.md §§13.1-13.2

Conflicting change approval rules: MSA requires any change to Services to be agreed in writing by both parties before implementation, while Change Control Procedure permits deemed approval by Customer silence and approval by Provider's Delivery Lead without Customer approval for cost impacts up to £35,000. 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §§4.2-4.4
Change Control Procedure references a Change Control Board in MSA clause 17, but the MSA has no clause 17. 08_change_control.md §4.1; 01_msa.md

Change Control Procedure permits change-related charges without ordinary charge-increase notice requirements, conflicting with MSA CPI/60-day limits for Fee increases where a change alters charges. 01_msa.md §4.4; 08_change_control.md §§5.1, 5.3

Change Control Procedure refers to an impact-assessment charge rate in the Exit and Transition Plan, but the Exit Plan contains only a transition-assistance day rate and no specific impact-assessment preparation rate. 08_change_control.md §7.2; 09_exit.md §3.2

Conflicting day rates: Pricing Schedule standard rate is £1,450 per person per day, Exhibit B sets lower role-specific rates for several roles, and Exit Plan transition assistance is £1,250 per person per day. 10_pricing.md §2.1; 14_exhibit_b_personnel.md §3; 09_exit.md §3.2
BCDR recovery site in Frankfurt is not listed in DPA Annex 2 approved processing locations, creating a conflict if Customer Personal Data is replicated there. 07_bcdr.md §3.1; 03_dpa.md Annex 2

BCDR excludes Continuity Event and return-to-primary unavailability from availability calculations and suspends SLA obligations, while the SLA availability calculation/exclusions do not include this carve-out. 07_bcdr.md §§5.1-5.3; 04_sla.md §§3.1-3.3, 9

BCDR Recovery Time Objective is measured from Provider's Invocation, but only Provider's Head of Operations may declare Invocation; delay or failure to invoke would delay or avoid the RTO starting. 07_bcdr.md §§1.5, 2.1, 4.1

Acceptable Use Policy allows Provider to amend the policy on 30 days' notice with continued use deemed acceptance, conflicting with the general requirement that changes to Services be agreed in writing by both parties and with the Change Control Procedure for changes to scope/timetable/charges/acceptance criteria. 11_acceptable_use.md §§8.1-8.2; 01_msa.md §2.4; 08_change_control.md §1.1

Acceptable Use Policy states Provider does not monitor Customer content and accepts no responsibility for it, which sits uneasily with DPA processor/security obligations requiring protection, access logging, assistance and incident handling for Customer Personal Data. 11_acceptable_use.md §4.1; 03_dpa.md §§2, 6, 7, 10

Acceptable Use Policy permits disclosure of Customer content to law enforcement or regulators without notifying Customer, while DPA requires Provider to process Customer Personal Data only on Customer's documented instructions and restricts Security Incident/public communications. 11_acceptable_use.md §§6.1-6.2; 03_dpa.md §§2.2, 6.3

Acceptable Use Policy prohibits storing payment card primary account numbers, while Information Security Policy classifies payment card data as Restricted Data and sets security controls for it, implying such data may be stored if protected. 11_acceptable_use.md §3.2; 06_infosec.md §§1.2, 3.1

Information Security Policy permits Customer data storage/processing in any Provider region selected by Provider's CISO with after-the-fact notice of new regions, conflicting with DPA prior-authorisation and approved-location restrictions. 06_infosec.md §§2.1-2.3; 03_dpa.md §§4.1-4.3

Glossary definition of Subprocessor covers any third party processing Personal Data, while DPA definition is limited to third parties processing Customer Personal Data; the scope of consent and flow-down obligations is therefore inconsistent. 03_dpa.md §1.5; 15_glossary.md §2

Glossary Business Day definition includes public holidays, which conflicts with MSA/SLA definitions and can alter notice, cure, support and reporting deadlines across the contract. 15_glossary.md §2; 01_msa.md §1.2; 04_sla.md §1.1

Glossary is maintained by Provider's Commercial Director and additions are handled as Change Control changes, but the Glossary also purports to override all other definitions; unilateral maintenance could effectively alter core contractual meanings. 15_glossary.md §§1.2, 4.1-4.2

Order Form ranks Addenda below Schedules, which would subordinate the DPA to operational schedules such as SLA, Information Security Policy and Subprocessor List even where those schedules conflict with data protection terms. 05_order_form.md §2.1; 03_dpa.md

Order Form service commencement date is 1 April 2027, but SOW programme commencement is 1 March 2027, creating uncertainty over when services, billing and service levels begin. 05_order_form.md §1.3; 02_sow.md §2.2
